Subject (in full) Electric posts removed by Japanese soldiers.
Made by D.S. Hanawa. Forwarded by Osmar Smith
Sir,
At 3.15 p.m. on 24.8.39, Mr. Richardson of the S.M.Works,
came to the station and reported that he saw several Japanese
in Military uniform, cut down two electric posts which were
half burned and not in use from Lane 171 Tongshan Road
(demolished houses) by means of a saw and removed same in a
Japanese Military motor-truck.
D.S. Hanawa and C.D.O. 257 attended but no witness could
be located who can supply the Police with any information re
the removal of electric posts.
The Japanese Gendarmerie on Pingliang Road has been
informed, who promised to make enquiries into this case.
Eggarson

先生，

1939年8月24日下午3时15分，上海公共租界工部局电气处 (S.M.Works) 的理查森先生 (Mr. Richardson) 来到岗亭报告称，他看见几名身穿军装的日本士兵，在唐山路171弄（已拆除的房屋）用锯子锯倒了两根半烧毁且不再使用的电线杆，并用一辆日本军用卡车将其运走。

花轮警佐 (D.S. Hanawa) 和第257号华籍侦探 (C.D.O. 257) 前往处理，但未能找到能向警方提供有关拆除电线杆任何信息的证人。

SHANGHAI [MERCURY] & MERCURY.

15 - 7 / 3

JUL 1 1939

Nippon Soldiers
Loot Properties

Fractional Repayments
From Japanese
Offered

Still hoping to get compensation for their Point Island property looted and destroyed by the Japanese forces, foreign former tenants of the island have recently held further meetings to consider an offer of part payment made by the Nipponese. Some German tenants are reported to have accepted sums which represent but a fraction of their losses but it is not likely that many others will do the same.
The Japanese offer does not include movable property, which is the most valuable parts of the various claims, and which several tenants actually saw Japanese soldiers removing in trucks. The soldiers looted practically everything from the bungalows, including refrigerators and motor-cars. What they did not take away they destroyed. The compensation offer does not include boats, one of which, a former SMC firefloat, was recently seen in the Point Canal, used as a hulk by the military.
Thirty Percent
Many people were living on the island at the start of the hostilities. There were some beautiful bungalows. There were some shacks, perfectly adequate for residence. None of the buildings, comparatively speaking, cost much. The valuable part of the property was the fittings, furniture and personal effects. With electric light laid on, many people had refrigerators, expensive radios and other fittings. Many kept all their personal belongings in their bungalows.
The present Japanese offer is said to be for compensation for the "immovable" property they have confiscated and are using, not for the stuff looted in October, 1937, and is reported to be about 60 percent of the value claimed in dollars, "because Japanese army contractors estimate lower than civilian contractors." And, as the claims were made in sterling at an exchange of fourteen pence, double today's exchange, the Japanese offer works out at 80 percent, and that for the least valuable part of the property. Claims in other currencies, incidentally, were on the level of sterling.

C 8 / 7

1939年7月1日

日本士兵
掠夺财产

日本人提出的
部分赔偿方案

前岛上的外籍前租户仍希望就其被日军部队掠夺和摧毁的岛屿财产获得赔偿，最近再次举行会议，审议日本人提出的部分付款提议。据报道，一些德国租户已接受了仅占其损失一小部分的金额，但不太可能有其他许多人会这样做。

日方的提议不包括动产，而动产是各项索赔中最有价值的部分，且有几位租户亲眼目睹日本士兵用卡车运走这些物品。士兵们几乎洗劫了平房中的所有物品，包括冰箱和汽车。他们没拿走的东西则予以销毁。赔偿提议也不包括船只，其中一艘前工部局消防船最近被人看到在岛上的河道中，被军方用作废船壳。

百分之三十

战事开始时，岛上居住着许多人。那里有一些漂亮的平房。也有一些棚屋，完全适合居住。相对而言，没有任何建筑物花费巨大。财产中有价值的部分是装置、家具和个人物品。由于通了电灯，许多人拥有冰箱、昂贵的收音机和其他装置。许多人将所有个人财物都存放在他们的平房里。

据说，目前日本提出的报价是针对他们没收并正在使用的“不动产”的赔偿，而不是针对1937年10月被掠夺的物品，据报道约为以美元计算的索赔价值的60%，“因为日本军队承包商的估价低于民用承包商。”此外，由于索赔是以英镑提出，汇率为十四便士，是今日汇率的两倍，因此日本的提议折算下来相当于80%，但这仅是针对财产中价值最低的部分。顺便提一下，其他货币的索赔也与英镑水平相当。

Lile 2/7
C 8 / 7

page_data.en:
20252

October Looting
The island was evacuated by residents around August 17 and 18, 1937. Tenants who managed to get back later and remove a little of their property found it intact. But at the beginning of October, tenants saw three Japanese military lorries, under the charge of an officer, filled with furniture and personal effects in the process of being looted. Some people actually recognized their own property on the truck.
The officer was asked about this looting. He said that he was sorry that he had allowed his men to be a little careless, and that he would be more careful in future.

Caravan
Later on Major-General A. P. D Telfer-Smollett arranged a visit for tenants. Passes were obtained and signed by the general commanding the Japanese army here and by the admiral commanding the navy. At the Ting-hai Road bridge to the island, however, the caravan of 50 cars was refused admission....by a lance-corporal.
One man who arrived a little early managed to drive past the sentry and get to his bungalow. Here two soldiers were opening one of his trunks with a bayonet. While he stood there they carried all its contents out to a truck, bowing politely to the tenant each time they passed him. Then a patrol arrested the tenant and took him to the mainland. After an hour and a half they decided he was not a dangerous character and took him back to the bungalow ...where he found that his car had been stolen in the interim.

Visit In 1939
A group of tenants were allowed to inspect their property early this year. The scene was pathetic. Every bungalow had even its panelling torn out. Nothing was left, except a few fragments of documents, personal photographs and the like. One man even lost his wartime sword and medals.
Japanese pretenses at one time were said to be that the movable property had been taken by Chinese. But the tenants have no illusions over the matter. The Japanese army did the looting and damage. By their latest decision they have decided to leave their claims in the hands of their consulates, with instruction to keep on demanding full settlement for all property, at the fourteen pence sterling exchange level.

20252

十月劫掠

居民于1937年8月17日和18日左右撤离该岛。后来设法返回并搬走少量财产的租户发现其财产完好无损。但在10月初，租户们看到三辆日本军用卡车，由一名军官指挥，装满了正在被掠夺的家具和个人物品。有些人实际上在卡车上认出了自己的财产。

有人就此次劫掠质问该军官。他说，他很抱歉让手下有些疏忽，以后会更加小心。

车队

后来，A. P. D 特尔弗-斯莫利特少将 (Major-General A. P. D Telfer-Smollett) 为租户安排了一次参观。通行证由驻此地的日本陆军司令和日本海军司令签署。然而，在通往该岛的定海路桥头，这支由50辆汽车组成的车队被一名下士拒绝入内……

一名稍早到达的人设法驾车穿过哨兵，到达了他的平房。在这里，两名士兵正用刺刀打开他的一个行李箱。当他站在那里时，他们将箱内所有物品搬到一辆卡车上，每次经过租户时都礼貌地鞠躬。随后，巡逻队逮捕了该租户并将他带往大陆。一个半小时后，他们认定他并非危险人物，便将他送回平房……在那里他发现他的汽车在此期间已被盗。

1939年的参观

今年年初，一群租户获准检查他们的财产。景象令人伤感。每栋平房的护墙板甚至都被拆走。除了一些文件碎片、个人照片等外，什么都没留下。一个人甚至丢失了他的战时佩剑和勋章。

日本人曾一度声称动产是被中国人拿走的。但租户们对此不抱幻想。是日本军队进行了抢劫和破坏。根据他们最新的决定，他们已决定将索赔事宜交由各自领事馆处理，并指示继续要求按十四便士的英镑汇率对所有财产进行全额结算。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
Hongkew S. M. P. REGISTRY
No. S. P. Station,
REPORT
Date March 4th. 19 39.

Subject... Breaking of wooden door at the rear of No.14 Boone Road, (Registered
British property), by members of the Japanese Naval Landing Party.

Made by D. C. I. Crowther Forwarded by [Signature] c/t

Sir,

At 10.25 a.m. on the 4/3/39, Hari Singh, private watchman,
employed by Edward Nissim & Co. Ltd., Glen Line Building, No.2
Peking Road, Registered British Company, came to the Hongkew
Police Station and reported that an officer and another naval
rating of the Japanese Naval Landing Party, had broken into a
godown, situated at No.14 Boone Road, which is included in the
block of property at Boone and Fearon Roads, and Broadway, and
for which Edward Nissim & Co. Ltd. are agents.

J. D. C. No. 209 Masuda, and the undersigned, immediately
proceeded to the scene with the private watchman, and there met
Mr. K. Takata, and a marine of the J.N.L. Party.

Mr. K. Takata is employed in the Special Civilian Section
of the J.N.L. Party.

At this time Mr. K. Takata with the assistance of another
Japanese civilian was repairing the lower panel of a wooden door,
which gives access to a side alleyway that runs North to South
off a main alleyway, at the rear of No.14 Boone Road.

Mr. K. Takata explained to J.D.C. No.209 Masuda, that they
had made an investigation at the rear of No.14 Boone Road, and
to gain entry into the said alleyway had broken the lower panel
of the door. No entry had been made to the godown.

The undersigned communicated by telephone with Mr. Edward
Nissim, and following an explanation of the occurrence, he stated
that he was satisfied with the action taken and as there had been
nothing removed from the property he would not take any further
action.

D.O."C" informed.

[Signature]
Crowther

日期：1939年3月4日。

事由……日本海军陆战队队员破坏布恩路14号（注册为英国财产）后部的木门。

制作人：克罗瑟侦探长 (D. C. I. Crowther) 转呈人：[签名] c/t

先生，

1939年3月4日上午10时25分，受雇于北京路2号格兰线大楼 (Glen Line Building) 爱德华·尼西姆有限公司 (Edward Nissim & Co. Ltd.)（注册英国公司）的私人看守哈里·辛格 (Hari Singh) 来到虹口警察局报告称，日本海军陆战队的一名军官和另一名水兵闯入位于布恩路14号的仓库，该仓库属于布恩路、费伦路 (Fearon Roads) 和百老汇路街区的财产，爱德华·尼西姆有限公司为其代理人。

第209号日籍侦探长 (J. D. C.) 增田 (Masuda) 和本人立即随同私人看守前往现场，并在那里遇到了高田先生 (Mr. K. Takata) 和一名日本海军陆战队队员。

高田先生受雇于日本海军陆战队的特别民事部门。

当时，高田先生在另一名日本平民的协助下，正在修理布恩路14号后部一扇木门的下部镶板，该门通向一条从主巷向北向南延伸的侧巷。

高田先生向第209号日籍侦探长增田解释说，他们对布恩路14号后部进行了调查，为了进入上述巷道，他们破坏了门的下部镶板。并未进入仓库。

本人与爱德华·尼西姆先生通电话，在解释事件经过后，他表示对采取的行动感到满意，并且由于财产中没有任何物品被移走，他将不再采取进一步行动。

已通知“C”区侦探长。

[签名]
克罗瑟 (Crowther)

CHINA PRESS.
JAN 29 1939

Point Island
Property In
Nippon Hands

Negotiations Continue,
But Position Said
Unsatisfactory

BUILDINGS LOOTED,
HOUSES DESOLATE

Visit By Owners “Like
Military Procession”
After Landing

More than 18 months after the cessation of hostilities in the vicinity of Shanghai, Point Island, former holiday resort of Shanghailanders, is still totally in the hands of the Japanese military and naval authorities, it was learned yesterday by THE CHINA PRESS.

Strong protests by foreign property owners on the Island notwithstanding, the Japanese authorities have absolutely refused to hand back land and houses, and have further prevented owners from inspecting their property except under strict military supervision.

“Wilful Damage”

Three or four parties of property owners, most of them members of the Minghong or Shanghai Yacht Club, it is reported, have been permitted to make one of these conducted tours of the Island under supervision, and have returned to Shanghai with stories of houses desolated, in dreadful state of disrepair, and thoroughly looted or wilfully damaged.

One property owner reported that panels which had formerly graced the rooms of his country residence had been removed, while what furniture remained had been battered about with some sort of blunt instruments, apparently rifle butts.

“Our houses, such as they are,” said another owner, “are little more than walls with a roof above them. Nothing has been spared.”

“Conducted visits to private houses are just like military parades,” declared another owner. “After we had landed, we were surrounded by soldiers on foot and on motor-cycles, and we were permitted to look neither to the right nor to the left. We saw what was left of our property and then returned to Shanghai.”

Offer Unconfirm.

Reports that the Japanese authorities had offered at least one owner a percentage of the compensation asked by him provided that he would deal directly with the Japanese authorities instead of through his consulate could not be confirmed yesterday, but it was stated by one member of the Point Island Property Owners’ Association that no member could possibly agree to such an action.

Negotiations for the return to foreign owners of property on Point Island were launched some time ago, but the position is still regarded in diplomatic circles as the most unsatisfactory of all negotiations undertaken regarding foreign rights in China.

Protests In Tokyo

British, American, and French authorities both in Shanghai and Tokyo have lodged claims, accompanied by strenuous protests, but so far, without result.

It is believed by a number of property owners on the Island that the Japanese authorities are attempting to “squeeze” foreigners out in order to establish a large-scale military and naval base there.

This theory, according to several individuals who were included in the conducted tours to the Island, was supported by their observations there. “The Island,” it was reported, “was alive with soldiers.”

Japan To Take Census
Of All Gold Articles

TOKYO, Jan. 28.—(Reuters)—The Ministry of Finance is seeking legal powers to take a census of all gold articles, preparatory to compelling their owners to sell to the Government in case of necessity.

《字林西报》(CHINA PRESS)。
1939年1月29日

点岛 (Point Island)
财产落入
日本人之手

谈判仍在继续，
但据称局势
令人不满

建筑物遭劫掠，
房屋荒废

业主参观“如同
军事游行”
登陆之后

据《字林西报》昨日获悉，在上海周边地区停战18个多月后，曾是上海外侨度假胜地的点岛，仍完全处于日本军事和海军当局的控制之下。

尽管岛上的外籍业主强烈抗议，日本当局断然拒绝归还土地和房屋，并进一步阻止业主检查其财产，除非在严格的军事监督下进行。

“故意破坏”

据报道，有三四批业主（大多是明宏俱乐部或上海游艇俱乐部的成员）获准在监督下对该岛进行一次引导式参观，他们回到上海后讲述了房屋荒废、破损严重、被彻底洗劫或故意破坏的情况。

一位业主报告说，曾经装饰其乡间住宅房间的护墙板已被拆除，而剩余的家具则被某种钝器（显然是枪托）砸坏。

另一位业主说：“我们的房子，也就那样，只不过是有屋顶的墙壁而已。什么都没能幸免。”

又一位业主宣称：“对私人房屋的‘引导式参观’就像军事阅兵一样。我们登陆后，被步行和骑摩托车的士兵包围，我们不被允许向左或向右看。我们看到了剩下的财产，然后就回到了上海。”

提议未经证实。

关于日本当局已向至少一名业主提出按其索赔金额的一定比例进行赔偿，条件是他直接与日本当局打交道而非通过其领事馆的报道，昨日无法得到证实，但点岛业主协会的一名成员表示，任何成员都不可能同意此类做法。

关于将点岛财产归还给外籍业主的谈判已在一段时间前启动，但在外交界看来，这一局势仍是所有涉及在华外籍权益的谈判中最令人不满的。

在东京提出抗议

英国、美国和法国当局在上海和东京均提出了索赔，并伴随强烈的抗议，但迄今毫无结果。

岛上许多业主认为，日本当局正试图将外国人“挤走”，以便在那里建立大型军事和海军基地。

据几位参加岛内引导式参观的人士称，他们的观察支持了这一理论。据报道，“岛上到处都是士兵。”

日本将对所有黄金制品
进行普查

东京，1月28日。（路透社）——财政部正在寻求法律授权，以便对所有黄金制品进行普查，为在必要时强制所有者将其出售给政府做准备。

（右上角框内文字：历史 / 编号 S. B. D. / 日期 .）
（右下角手写批注：档案 C 20/7）

Wayside Station,
REPORT
Date Nov. 18, 38.
19
Subject Alleged removal of furniture by two Japanese.
Made by J.D.S. Hanawa. Forwarded by [Signature] [Signature]

Sir,
At 12.05 p.m. 18.11.38 a Chinese female named Tsang Tsou Dee, age 34, residing at 124 Kungping Fong, Kungping Road in the employ of Kong Ei Co. as a watchman, came to this station and reported that at about 11.55 a.m. same date, two Japanese believed to be Naval employees entered House No.26 Lane 225 Kungping Road which is an unoccupied house at present, attempting to remove a broken gramophone record file and broken hat stand therefrom.

Upon receipt of this report, J.P.C. 194 and C.D.C. 291 immediately proceeded to the above place, however, they had already decamped the alleyway in question before the arrival of Police leaving the above property outside the back door of the premises. Nothing was removed by the Japanese. The under-signed informed the Consular Police of this case and Consular Police Constable Nakagawa attended this station. Accompanied by Mr. Nakagawa the undersigned and C.D.C. 291 visited the premises in question and instituted enquiries.

Tsang Tsou Dee stated that at 12.05 p.m. 18.11.38, she saw two Japanese entered the alleyway whereupon she followed them and found that the Japanese was removing the said property from House No.26 in the same alleyway. She became frightened, and reported the matter to this station.

The premises was securely locked and the property in question was put into the premises by Mr. Mr. Nakagawa stated that he will inform this matter to the Gendarmerie and Naval Landing Party to take appropriate measure to prevent such occurrence in future and to make enquiries into this case.

[Signature]
Senior Det 1/c
D.D.O. "D"

[Signature]
J.D.S. 157.

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
杂项档案号 213/38。
路边巡捕房，
报告
日期：1938年11月18日。
19
事由：据称两名日本人搬走家具。
报告人：J.D.S. Hanawa。转呈人：[签名] [签名]

敬启者：
1938年11月18日下午12时05分，一名名为Tsang Tsou Dee（音译）的34岁中国女性，居住于公平路公平坊124号，受雇于Kong Ei Co.（音译）担任看守，来到本巡捕房报案称，同日约上午11时55分，两名据信为海军雇员的日本人进入了公平路225弄26号房屋，该房屋目前无人居住，他们试图从屋内搬走一个破损的留声机唱片架和一个破损的帽架。

接到此报告后，J.P.C. 194号和C.D.C. 291号警员立即前往上述地点，然而，在警察到达之前，他们已逃离该弄堂，将上述物品遗留在该处后门之外。日本人未拿走任何物品。具名报告人将此案通报给领事警察，领事警察中川（Nakagawa）警员来到本巡捕房。由中川先生陪同，具名报告人和C.D.C. 291号警员走访了涉事房屋并展开调查。

Tsang Tsou Dee（音译）陈述称，1938年11月18日下午12时05分，她看见两名日本人进入弄堂，于是她跟随他们，发现日本人正在同一弄堂的26号房屋内搬走上述物品。她感到害怕，遂向本巡捕房报告此事。

该房屋门锁完好，涉事物品已被中川先生放回屋内。中川先生表示，他将把此事通报给宪兵队和海军陆战队，采取适当措施防止此类事件再次发生，并对本案进行调查。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
Misc. File No. 211/38.
No. Seward Road Station,
17th Nov. 1938.

REPORT

Subject Removal of Furniture from Houses in Sih Woo Li off Kungping
Road by Civilian Japanese.

Made by D.S.I. Gigarson, Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,
At 4.20 p.m. on the 17-11-38, one named Wong Ying Sung
(王英忠), age 36, residing, 3 Wei S Fong off Ningpo Road,
came to Station and reported that some unknown persons had
removed his furniture from 24 Sih Woo Li off Kungping Road,
his former residence, and had placed the above furniture in the
alleyway, ready for removal.

F.S. Rosanoff proceeded to the above address on Kungping
Road and located some witnesses who stated that they had seen
civilian Japanese removing the furniture from the houses situat-
ed in the Sih Woo Li alleyway.

At 5.45 p.m., even date, F.S. Rosanoff whilst on M/Cycle
patrol saw a male Japanese removing from the above alleyway a
bedstead, but the Japanese threw the bedstead away and then
attempted to run away being chased by F.S. Rosanoff, who effect-
ed the arrest of the Japanese. Whilst on the way to Station
on Seward Road the Japanese struggled with F.S. Rosanoff, who
was wearing gloves and the Japanese managed to slip out of his
jacket, leaving same and a Khaki Japanese style cap in the hands
of F.S. Rosanoff and made good his escape.

Enquiries were made by D.S. Hanawa and the undersigned.
The Japanese Consular Police was informed and Sergeant G. Kiku-
chi attended this Station. The case was explained to him and
he was also informed that other complaints of the same nature
had been received at this Station. Sergeant Kikuchi stated
that he will hand over the case to the Japanese Military Police
for enquiries and action. The Khaki jacket and cap were handed
over to the above representative of the Japanese Consular Police
upon signing the Detained Property Book for the property.

D.D.O. "D" [Signature]
Sen. Dkt. i/c
[Signature]
D.S.I.

西华德路巡捕房，
1938年11月17日。

报告

事由：平民日本人从公平路旁四和里（Sih Woo Li）的房屋中搬走家具。

报告人：D.S.I. Gigarson，转呈人：[签名]

敬启者：
1938年11月17日下午4时20分，一名名为Wong Ying Sung（王英忠），36岁，居住于宁波路旁Wei S Fong（音译）3号的男子，来到巡捕房报案称，一些不明身份的人将其家具从他以前居住的公平路旁四和里（Sih Woo Li）24号搬出，并将上述家具放置在弄堂内，准备运走。

F.S. Rosanoff 前往公平路的上述地址，找到了一些证人，他们陈述称曾看见平民日本人从位于四和里弄堂内的房屋中搬走家具。

同日下午5时45分，F.S. Rosanoff 在骑摩托车巡逻时，看见一名日本男子正从上述弄堂搬出一张床架，但该日本人扔下床架，随后试图逃跑，F.S. Rosanoff 随即追赶并将其逮捕。在前往西华德路巡捕房的途中，该日本人与戴着皮手套的 F.S. Rosanoff 搏斗，该日本人设法从其夹克中挣脱，将夹克和一顶卡其色日式帽子留在 F.S. Rosanoff 手中，成功逃脱。

D.S. Hanawa 和具名报告人进行了调查。已通知日本领事警察，菊池（G. Kikuchi）警长来到本巡捕房。向他说明了案情，并告知他本巡捕房还收到过其他同类投诉。菊池警长表示，他将把此案移交给日本宪兵队进行调查和处理。在签署扣押财产登记簿后，卡其色夹克和帽子已移交给上述日本领事警察代表。

高级侦探长
[签名]

Date Nov. 11th, 1938.

REPORT

Subject Letter from Land Bank of China (Property Department) C.R.F. 2900/1906.

Made by D. S. I. Kennedy Forwarded by Insp. B. Malone

Sir,
With reference to the above mentioned letter, the undersigned and P.C.I. Sun H. Poh proceeded to Lane 55 Sungpan Road this A.M. and made the following enquiries. Houses 41 to 47 in this row have been intact up till about the end of October, when a Japanese civilian accompanied by a squad of Chinese coolies commenced to systematically remove the bricks from the walls of the houses mentioned. This row of houses is still standing however but all the fittings, doors, window frames, etc. have been removed, and big gaps are noticeable in the walls where the bricks have been removed. The same applies to four houses- numbers of which have been obliterated, which are the only ones left standing in the next block, Nos. 71-74. The remainder of the houses in the last mentioned block were completely destroyed by fire during the hostilities.

Two male Chinese named Lee Hu Ngan (李協直) and Yung Kung Sing (楊根兴) residing in the vicinity of Lane 55 Sungpan Road were located and on being questioned, stated that the bricks and fittings had been removed by a squad of Chinese coolies working under the supervision of a Japanese civilian. The bricks etc, which have been removed on various dates since the end of October, have been transported by motor truck, licence No. unknown, and a number of wheelbarrows were also used.

This is the first notification made to this station regarding their property, made by the Land Bank of China who have not even troubled to install a watchman to look after the premises, consequently even in the event of the removal of the property coming to notice of the Police at the actual time of

日期：1938年11月11日。

报告

事由：关于中国银行地产部（Property Department）来信，参考号 C.R.F. 2900/1906。

报告人：D. S. I. Kennedy，转呈人：Insp. B. Malone

敬启者：
关于上述来信，具名报告人和 P.C.I. Sun H. Poh（音译）于今晨前往松潘路55弄，并进行了如下调查。该排41至47号房屋直至10月底一直完好无损，当时一名平民日本人在一队中国苦力的陪同下，开始系统地拆除上述房屋墙壁上的砖块。这一排房屋仍然矗立，但所有装置、门、窗框等均已被拆除，墙壁上因砖块被拆而留下明显的巨大缺口。下一街区仅存的71-74号四栋房屋情况相同，其门牌号码已被抹去。该街区其余房屋在战事期间完全被大火烧毁。

找到了两名居住在松潘路55弄附近的中国男子，名为 Lee Hu Ngan（李協直）和 Yung Kung Sing（楊根兴），经询问，他们陈述称，砖块和装置是由一队在中国苦力在一位平民日本人的监督下拆除的。自10月底以来在不同日期拆下的砖块等物，已通过一辆车牌号不详的卡车以及多辆手推车运走。

这是中国银行就其财产向本巡捕房发出的首次通知，该行甚至未曾费心安装看守人员来照看房产，因此，即使在警方实际注意到财产被搬走的情况下……

Further REPORT
Wayside Station,
Date Oct. 31, 19 38.
Subject Re three employees of the Japanese Naval Construction Unit arrested
for breaking into the S.M.P. Paoting Road Quarters.
Made by D.S.I. Suhoff. Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,

When effecting the arrest of the three Japanese at Police
Quarters on Paoting Road it was noticed that several windows
were broken on each floor of the building. None of the Police
officers however saw any of the three arrested Japanese
actually break the windows. At 9 a.m. 31.10.38 S.I. Moore and
the undersigned inspected the Police quarters when it was
ascertained that in total 75 pans of glass were broken in the
windows of various flats of five floors. (The complete list of
damage done is attached hereto).

There is no Police posted at the quarters and owing to
a very easy access to the compound of the building over a low
wall, it appears that the quarters might have been entered by
looters, previously . However as the employees of the Naval
Construction Unit are now working on the adjoining vacant
piece of ground, they are strongly suspected to be responsible
for the damage and J.D.C. 157 Hanawa has been instructed to
inform the Japanese Gendarmerie of the occurrence requesting
them to question the 3 arrested men and make enquiries at the
Naval Construction Unit.

In the meantime one S.P.C. has been posted on the
premises.

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
[Signature]
D.S.I.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE SPECIAL BRANCH）

John Cady m!

日期：1938年10月31日。
事由：关于三名日本海军建设部队雇员因闯入工部局警务处保定路宿舍被捕一事。
报告人：D.S.I. Suhoff。转呈人：[签名]

敬启者：

在保定路警察宿舍逮捕三名日本人时，注意到该建筑每层楼都有几扇窗户破碎。然而，没有警官亲眼看见这三名被捕日本人中的任何一人实际打破窗户。1938年10月31日上午9时，S.I. Moore 和具名报告人检查了警察宿舍，查明五层楼各公寓的窗户总共打破了75块玻璃。（损坏完整清单附后）。

宿舍没有派驻警察，且由于翻过低墙即可非常容易地进入大楼院落，似乎此前可能有窃贼进入过宿舍。然而，由于海军建设部队的雇员目前正在相邻的空地上工作，他们被强烈怀疑对损坏负责，已指示 J.D.C. 157 Hanawa 将此事件通报日本宪兵队，要求他们讯问这3名被捕男子，并在海军建设部队进行调查。

与此同时，已有一名特别巡捕（S.P.C.）派驻在该处。

此致，
敬礼，
[签名]
D.S.I.

REPORT
Date Oct. 30th, 19 38.
Subject Re three employees of the Japanese Naval Construction Unit arrested
for breaking into the S.M.P. Paoting Road Quarters.
Made by D.S.I. Suhoff, Forwarded by [签名]

Sir,
At 1.00 p.m. 30-10-38, a telephone message was received
at this Station from an unknown person , probably foreigner,
who refused to give his name, reporting that Japanese civilians
were breaking the windows of Paoting Road Police Quarters.
D.S. Rynstone, F.S.34 Kramer, J.P.C.129, C.D.C.76 and the
undersigned immediately attended and found the front door of
the premises in question in tact and examination around the
building revealed a bamboo ladder standing inside the compound
of the building near the wall facing South.
Climbing this ladder the aforementioned police officers
entered the Police Quarters and therein found three Japanese,
who questioned by J.P.C.129 gave their names as follows:-
(1) Takashi Kamura, age 25, Japanese,
(2) Tatsura Akagaki, age 25, Japanese,
(3) Takaichiro Okumura, age 28, Japanese,
all employed by the Japanese Naval Construction Unit.
The 2nd named was found to be, by D.S. Rynstone and F.S.
Kramer when arrested on the 1st floor of the building, in posses-
sion of 2 pairs of Police boots, whilst the 3rd named was found
by the two above mentioned officers and J.P.C.129 on the same
floor in possession of two pairs of Police boots and one pair
of old black leather shoes.
The 1st named was arrested in the same floor by the above
officers but he had nothing in his possession.
The three arrested Japanese were taken to this Station
where they were questioned by J.D.C.157 Hanawa when they admitted
having entered the building of the S.M.P. Chinese Quarters

报告人：D.S.I. Suhoff，转呈人：[签名]

敬启者：
1938年10月30日下午1时00分，本巡捕房接到一个未知人士（可能是外国人）的电话留言，此人拒绝透露姓名，报告称有平民日本人正在打破保定路警察宿舍的窗户。D.S. Rynstone、F.S.34 Kramer、J.P.C.129、C.D.C.76 和具名报告人立即赶往现场，发现涉事房屋的前门完好无损，对建筑物周围的检查显示，在大楼院内靠近南墙的墙边立着一架竹梯。
顺着这架梯子攀爬，上述警官进入了警察宿舍，并在里面发现了三名日本人，经 J.P.C.129 讯问，他们报出的姓名如下：
(1) Takashi Kamura（音译），25岁，日本人，
(2) Tatsura Akagaki（音译），25岁，日本人，
(3) Takaichiro Okumura（音译），28岁，日本人，
均受雇于日本海军建设部队。
D.S. Rynstone 和 F.S. Kramer 在逮捕第二名嫌疑人时，发现他在大楼一楼持有两双警用靴子；而上述两名警官和 J.P.C.129 在同一楼层发现第三名嫌疑人持有两双警用靴子和一双旧黑皮鞋。
第一名嫌疑人在同一楼层被上述警官逮捕，但他身上没有任何物品。
三名被捕的日本人被带到本巡捕房，由 J.D.C.157 Hanawa 进行讯问，他们承认进入了工部局警务处华籍职员宿舍大楼

Date October, 16th, 38.

Subject Re the breaking and entering of British property by members
of the Japanese Naval Operating Party.

Made by D.S.122 Tynstone, Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,

At 8.00 a.m. 16-10-38, a telephone message was received
from the Imperial Chemical Industries (China) Ltd., Godown
(British), No.233 Chaoufoong Road, reporting trouble with
Japanese.

On receipt of the telephone message, D.S.I. McCahey,
J.D.C.Hanawa, C.D.C.295 and the undersigned proceeded to the
above mentioned godown and therein interviewed Mr. L. Perry
(British Subject) with the result that the following was
ascertained.

Mr. Perry who incidently resides in the I.C.I. Godown,
No.233 Chaoufoong Road, was awoke at about 7.30 a.m. 16-10-38
by sounds created as if some person or persons were endea-
vouring to force open a door.

This resulted in Mr. Perry proceeding outside the godown
where he observed 7 male Japanese attired in Khaki hats, shirts
and pants enter No.723 East Seward Road (a vacant shop) via
the front door which they had forced open with a large wooden
pole.

Mr. Perry immediately remonstrated with the intruders
who departed from the premises via point of entry and proceeded
to East Seward Road and Chaoufoong Road corner where they
together with about 300 other male Japanese of the coolie type
are engaged in unloading wooden poles, etc., from Japanese
Military trucks.

Premises No.723 East Seward Road is the property of the
Imperial Chemical Industries, Ltd.,

The culprits in this case who could not be identified
are undoubtedly members of the Japanese Naval Operating Party

事由 关于日本海军作战部队成员闯入并侵入英国财产一事。

制作人 高级探员（D.S.）122号 廷斯通（Tynstone），转呈人 [签名]

先生，

1938年10月16日上午8时，接到来自兆丰路233号帝国化学工业（中国）有限公司仓库（英资）的电话留言，报告与日本人发生纠纷。

接到电话留言后，高级探员主管麦卡希（McCahey）、日本侦探主任花轮（Hanawa）、华人侦探主任（C.D.C.）295号及本人前往上述仓库，并在那里会见了L. 佩里（Perry）先生（英国臣民），结果查明以下情况。

佩里先生顺便提一下，居住在兆丰路233号帝国化学工业公司仓库内，于1938年10月16日上午7时30分左右被仿佛有人试图强行撬开门的声音吵醒。

这导致佩里先生走到仓库外，他观察到7名身穿卡其色帽子、衬衫和裤子的日本男子通过前门进入东华德路723号（一家空置店铺），他们用一根大木杆强行撬开了前门。

佩里先生立即向入侵者提出抗议，入侵者随后从进入点离开该处所，前往东华德路与兆丰路拐角处，在那里他们与大约300名其他苦力类型的日本男子一起，正从日本军用卡车上卸载木杆等物品。

东华德路723号处所为帝国化学工业有限公司的财产。

本案罪犯身份无法确认，但无疑是日本海军作战部队的成员

Para 3. points out that it is not good policy to lay hands on

The owners of the cotton in the mill in question are known,
and they request the S.M.C. as ratepayers to state the action

mill leased by them from the Hongkong Shanghai Banking Corporation.
The only protest made appears to have been made on 27-5-38 from

ese mills are working night and day.
Para 4. goes on to state that the police would be unwise to
lift restrictions and shut their eyes to the unlawful removal of
property, but it would be wise not to question the authority of
the Japanese Special Service Commission or Naval Landing Party.
In the Kung Dah Mill case after the first protest made in
connection with the pass issued by General Hayada to the Kung Dah
No. 2 Cotton Mill, the Police have not closed their eyes to the
theft but from information received are of the opinion that after
the cotton is taken to the Heng Foong Cotton Mill Godown 310 Wa-
shing Road it is transported to the Kung Dah No. 2 Mill for use.
The Police therefore could not be expected to co-operate in
the theft committed against S.M.C. ratepayers. Discretion has
therefore been used to keep the owners notified of the removal of
their property.

第3段指出，除非绝对军事必要要求没收或移除财产，否则染指他人财产，尤其是在所有权已知的情况下，并非良策。
涉事工厂棉花的所有者是已知的，他们作为纳税人请求工部局说明采取了何种行动，以防止他们从汇丰银行租赁的工厂内的棉花被大规模盗窃。似乎唯一的抗议是在1938年5月27日由耶尔德（Yeid.）警署提出的。既然日本工厂日夜开工，就不能声称有任何军事必要性。
第4段继续指出，警方解除限制并对非法移除财产视而不见是不明智的，但不质疑日本特别服务委员会或海军陆战队的权威则是明智之举。
在公大纱厂案中，在就林田（Hayada）将军向公大第二棉纱厂签发的通行证提出第一次抗议后，警方并未对盗窃行为视而不见，但根据收到的信息认为，棉花被运往华盛路310号恒丰棉纱厂仓库后，会被转运至公大第二纱厂使用。
因此，不能期望警方配合针对工部局纳税人的盗窃行为。因此，已酌情通知业主其财产被移除的情况。

Subject Report of Japanese entering premises at House No. 3 Lane 468 Haining
Road.
Made by D.S. Gibson Forwarded by J. S. Jenkins Inspector,
Officer i/c.

Sir,
On the 14/6/38 a.m. Mr. Philip Liang, residing at 12/1375
Yu Yuen Road, came to the station and reported that Japanese had
attempted to remove property from his home at 3/468 Haining
Road.
Enquiries by Dets. S. A. Chi Huang and D.S. Gibson.
3/468 Haining Road is a dwelling house situated near North
Szechuen Road and is in the sector controlled by Japanese
Authorities. The compt. evacuated at the commencement of
hostilities and the only occupant at present is a watchman,
Chang Tah Yuen (張德元). A considerable amount of furniture
and other effects is stored in the premises.
It was learned from the watchman that about 4.00 p.m.
13/6/38 two Japanese, dressed in foreign style civilian clothing,
had knocked at the door and on being admitted, stated they were
members of the Japanese Consulate and subsequently inspected
the premises.
After having picked a piano stored in the house the
Japanese stated that they would like to purchase the instrument
or that if the owner did not wish to sell they would like to
borrow the piano.
The watchman replied that his master was absent and that
he, the watchman, was not empowered to dispose of the property.
The two Japanese then went away.
The watchman informed the compt. by telephone on 14/6/38
resulting in the compt. coming to the station on 15/6/38 a.m.

J. Gibson.
D. S.

敬启者：
1938年6月14日上午，居住于愚园路1375弄12号的 Philip Liang 先生来到捕房报案，称有日本人试图从其位于海宁路468弄3号的家中搬走财物。
经警探 S. A. Chi Huang 和警佐 D.S. Gibson 调查。
海宁路468弄3号是一栋住宅，位于北四川路附近，处于日本当局控制的区域内。该住户在战事开始时已撤离，目前唯一的居住者是一名看守人，张德元（Chang Tah Yuen）。屋内储存有大量家具及其他物品。
据看守人称，1938年6月13日下午4时许，两名身穿西式便服的日本人敲门，获准进入后声称是日本领事馆成员，随后检查了该处所。
在查看了存放在屋内的一架钢琴后，日本人表示希望购买该乐器，或者如果主人不愿出售，他们希望借用这架钢琴。
看守人回答说他的主人不在，他作为看守人无权处置这些财产。随后两名日本人离开。
1938年6月14日，看守人通过电话通知了住户，导致住户于1938年6月15日上午来到捕房。

J. Gibson.

Sir,
At 9.20 a.m. May 7th Mr. Yourieff, representative of Belting and Leather Products Association, 57 Peking Road, came to the station and reported that Japanese were in the act of removing gravel from their building under construction on North East side of Lay Road Bridge off Pingliang Road.

J.D.S. Osano and the undersigned accompanied informant to the scene and found that the motortruck had already left with a load. However, a number of Japanese civilians were there with shovels and who, when questioned, admitted that they were assisting in the removal of gravel. They further stated that the trucks (two) would return soon.

A few minutes later two trucks returned and one H. Goto, civilian stated he had been instructed by the J.N.L. Party at China Merchants Lower Wharf to transport gravel to those premises for use on a new building under construction.

On being informed they were removing American property over which the American flag was flying Goto stated he was obeying instructions but would accompany Police to the China Merchants Lower Wharf where the Officer i/c could be interviewed.

Sub-Lieut. Shimada i/c of a new construction on the China Merchants Lower Wharf admitted having given orders for the transportation of the building material but at the time was not aware it was American property.

Lieut Shimada was then informed that the American flag was flying over the partially built building on Pingliang Road and that these removals of sand, gravel

5月7日上午9时20分，北京路57号皮带皮革制品协会代表 Yourieff 先生来到捕房报案，称日本人正在平凉路赖氏路桥东北侧其在建建筑物处搬运碎石。

J.D.S. Osano 和本人陪同报案人前往现场，发现载货卡车已装载货物离开。然而，现场有多名手持铁锹的日本平民，经询问，他们承认正在协助搬运碎石。他们还表示两辆卡车很快会返回。

几分钟后，两辆卡车返回，一名名为 H. Goto 的平民称，他受招商局下码头日本海军陆战队指示，将碎石运往那些场所以供新建建筑使用。

当被告知他们正在搬运悬挂美国国旗的美国财产时，Goto 表示他是在服从命令，但愿意陪同警察前往招商局下码头，以便向主管警官说明情况。

负责招商局下码头新建工程的岛田少尉承认曾下达运输建筑材料的命令，但当时并不知道那是美国财产。

随后告知岛田中尉，平凉路部分建成的建筑物上悬挂着美国国旗，且沙子、碎石的搬运工作

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.
Detention of two British Subjects and one American Citizen by the Japanese Naval Landing Party.
Sir,
At 6.30 a.m. on the 5/5/38, information was received by Japanese detectives attached to this station that members of the Japanese Naval Landing Party, 36th Division, stationed in the Kung Dah Cotton Mill, Whashing Road, in conjunction with the Japanese Consular Police were going to operate in a house to house search in the Eastern area of the International Settlement, East of Yuenchang Road.
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE - 6 MAY 1938 SPECIAL BRANCH）
At 8.40 a.m. on the 5/5/38, Chief Warrant Officer Onishi came to Hongkew Police Station and requested the assistance of a Japanese and foreign detectives, as they had found three foreigners in No. 9 Yuenchang Road whom they wished to be interrogated.
D.S.I. Watanabe and the undersigned proceeded to No. 9 Yuenchang Road and in a front room on the 1st floor found the following persons.
Mr. J.A. Barnes, aged 39 years, British subject, unemployed, not registered at the H.B.M. Consulate for 4 or 5 years.
Mr. C. Kemmett, aged 66 years, unemployed master mariner, British subject, registered at the H.B.M. Consulate.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE - 6 MAY 1938 SPECIAL BRANCH）

Sir,

Further to search conducted in Wayside District upon foreign occupied premises during the morning of 5.5.38, foreign occupied premises in Lane 130 off Kungping Road were also searched at the same time.

This search was concluded shortly after 9.00 a.m. when members of the Japanese Naval Land Party were withdrawn, during which period 34 male Chinese and 5 female Chinese were brought to Wayside Station for non possession of "passes", who were later escorted by S.M.Police to the Garden Bridge.

In connection with this searching of foreign premises, three complaints were recorded at Wayside Police Station by foreigners of non Russian nationality.

1. Mr. A.E. Ferris, British, residing Lane 130/3 Baikal Road together with his family including his sister-in-law, Mrs. Cooper (British).

Despite production of British passport search was continued by a Russian Speaking Japanese civilian, boxes and drawers being ransacked, passport being ignored.

Japanese officer present very courteous, search being carried out by Japanese civilians.

2. Mrs. Hill, Russian by birth, British by marriage, living 69 Baikal Road, search of premises by Japanese Marines.

Mrs. Hill is living together with a Russian male, the only occupants of the premises.

3. Mr. I.G. Remedios, Spanish, living Lane 144/30/32 Wayside Road, continued search of premises despite production of passport.

先生，

继1938年5月5日上午在韦斯特区对外籍人士占用的物业进行的搜查之后，同一时间也对公平路（Kungping Road）130弄内的外籍人士占用物业进行了搜查。

此次搜查在上午9点过后不久结束，当时日本海军陆战队员撤离，在此期间，34名中国男性和5名中国女性因未持有“通行证”被带至韦斯特区警局，随后由上海公共租界工部局警务处警察护送至外白渡桥。

关于此次对外籍人士居所的搜查，韦斯特区警局记录了三起非俄国籍外籍人士的投诉。

1. A.E. Ferris 先生，英国人，居住在贝加尔路（Baikal Road）130弄3号，与其家人包括其嫂 Cooper 夫人（英国人）同住。

尽管出示了英国护照，一名讲俄语的日本平民仍继续搜查，翻乱了箱子和抽屉，对护照置之不理。

在场的日本军官非常礼貌，搜查由日本平民执行。

2. Hill 夫人，出生时为俄罗斯人，婚后为英国人，居住在贝加尔路69号，日本海军陆战队员对其居所进行了搜查。

Hill 夫人与一名俄罗斯男性同住，他们是该居所的唯一居住者。

3. I.G. Remedios 先生，西班牙人，居住在韦斯特路（Wayside Road）144弄30/32号，尽管出示了护照，对其居所的搜查仍在继续。

当在华德路（Ward Road）和兆丰路（Chusan Road）进行搜查时

Sir,

At 6.00 a.m. 5.5.38 a strong detachment of members of the
Japanese Naval Landing Party (Marines) in charge of a number
officers, accompanied by Japanese in plain clothes proceeded
to search foreign type dwelling houses in Ward Road at the
rear of Wayside Station, Ward Road and Chusan Road.

The majority of these dwelling houses are occupied by
Russians, the various rooms of the premises being sub-let
to Russians.

This search was supposed due to the fact that the Japanese
authorities had information that Chinese terrorists were being
supplied with ammunition by Russians, which ammunition had been
found by the Russians from the scene of the early Sino Japanese
hostilities in the Eastern area.

Other detachments of Japanese Marines were also searching
premises in the Wayside Road, Baikal Road area, the detachment
being divided into several parties.

This search was being continued at 8.00 a.m. 5.5.38,
whilst sentries are posted in the area for examination of the
"passes" of all Chinese who are proceeding to their respective
employments.

At 5.30 a.m. 5.5.38, an officer of the Japanese Naval
Landing Party requested the service of Japanese Police to act
as interpreters during an examination of Chinese residents
permits in Wayside District. (J.P.C. 136 & J.P.C. 245 detailed.)

No assistance rendered by S.M. Police in regard to entry
of premises or assisting in search, J.D.C. Hanawa however being
requested on several occasions to act as an interpreter for
members of the Japanese Forces engaged in this searching.

C. 5/5. 28 s/s

先生，

1938年5月5日上午6时，一支由多名军官指挥的日本海军陆战队（海军陆战队员）强力分队， accompanied by 便衣日本人，前往韦斯特区警局后方的华德路、华德路和兆丰路一带，搜查西式住宅房屋。

这些住宅大多由俄罗斯人居住，各房间转租给俄罗斯人。

此次搜查据称是因为日本当局获悉有情报称，俄罗斯人正在向中国恐怖分子提供弹药，这些弹药是俄罗斯人在东部地区早期中日敌对行动现场发现的。

其他日本海军陆战队分队也在搜查韦斯特路、贝加尔路地区的物业，该分队被分成几个小组。

截至1938年5月5日上午8时，搜查仍在继续，同时在该地区部署了哨兵，检查所有前往各自工作地点的中国人的“通行证”。

1938年5月5日上午5时30分，日本海军陆战队的一名官员请求日本警察提供服务，在韦斯特区检查中国居民许可证期间担任翻译。（指派日本警察通讯员 136 号和 245 号。）

上海公共租界工部局警务处在进入居所或协助搜查方面未提供任何援助，但花轮（Hanawa）日本警察通讯员多次被要求为参与此次搜查的日本部队成员担任翻译。

was experienced during these enquiries the conversation was carried on in Shanghai dialect in which the marines were not very efficient. After remaining in the house for about 20 minutes they left and were accompanied to the alleyway gate by the watchman. On opening the gate the watchman saw two other Japanese, dressed in khaki cloth caps (military style), white shirts, khaki breeches, puttees and boots, standing outside a shop No.7 of this alleyway. They had by their sides several glass and wooden frames which had been removed from No.7. On seeing these two Japanese the marines referred to them as 'Lah Li Loony' and asked the watchman if he allowed them to take property away. The watchman replied that he did not interfere with Japanese. The marines then suggested that he received cumshaw from these people and when this was denied they told him to go back to his house and to shut the gate. This he did and remained there until a little after 5.p.m. when he left the lane and proceeded to his employers' office. When leaving the lane he noted that wooden frames had disappeared from outside shop No.7.

At 6.30.a.m. on 23.4.1938 he returned to duty and when inspecting the various premises under his charge he discovered that about 20 glass and wooden window frames and shutters had been removed from house No.4.

您忠实的仆人，

副督察。

副总监备注：
观察到该卡车由一名日本平民驾驶，并有数名中国苦力陪同。当就搬走这批价值相当高的财产的权利提出质疑时，司机跑进工厂并叫来两名日本士兵。随着士兵的出现，为防止非法搬走而未采取进一步行动，否则将发生事件。

Yangtzepoo Station,
REPORT
Date December 15, 19 37
Subject Incidents resulting from Sino-Japanese Hostilities in
Yangtzepoo District.
Made by D.S.I. McCahay Forwarded by [签名]

Sir,

At 1.15pm. December 13th. Private Indian Watchman
Karm Singh, employed at the Tiang Sung Woo Kee Leather
Tannery, 2545 Pingliang Road, reported that at 1pm. four
Japanese soldiers had entered the office of the Tannery
and took away a Typewriter, makers name or number un-
known.

These premises have been entered by Japanese troops
on previous occasions and steel safes broken and building
thoroughly looted.

At 1.30 pm. December 14th. Japanese troops handed
over to Yangtzepoo Station six male Chinese refugees
to be escorted over the Garden Bridge.

Questioned, these men stated that they were natives
of Wusih and that they had been pressed into labour
service by the Japanese on arrival of those soldiers at
Wusih. They had received nothing but food during their
employment.

All six were escorted over the Garden Bridge.

Yours obediently,
[签名]
D.S.I.

[签名]
D.I.O. "D". Div.
[签名]
Officer i/c Special Branch. ✓

阁下，

12月13日下午1时15分。受雇于平凉路2545号天盛吴记皮革鞣制厂（Tiang Sung Woo Kee Leather Tannery）的印度私人更夫卡姆·辛格（Karm Singh）报告称，下午1时，四名日本士兵进入鞣制厂办公室，拿走了一台打字机，制造商名称或编号不详。

此前日军曾多次进入该处所，砸开钢制保险箱，并对建筑物进行了彻底洗劫。

12月14日下午1时30分。日军向杨树浦捕房移交了六名中国男性难民，要求护送至外白渡桥。

经讯问，这些人称他们是无锡人，日军抵达无锡时将他们强征为劳工。在受雇期间，除食物外未获得任何报酬。

六人均被护送至外白渡桥。

Made by Rhodes. Forwarded by
Sir,
At 12.30.p.m. 4.12.37 a fire of unknown origin broke out
at Lane 364 Wardly Road, two Chinese dwelling houses were
completely destroyed by fire, and three others were partly
destroyed. Japanese troops are billeted in the near vicinity
but they were unable to advance any information as to the cause
of the out-break. The S.F.Brigade attended and functioned.
(Please see Misc 520/37 f.Rd.)
During the afternoon of the 4.12.37 Japanese troops again
took over the former Womens Home Chasning Road and are now
using the premises as a billet. The owners were informed of
this occupation.
During the afternoon of the 4.12.37 a party of Japanese
Marines were observed closing and nailing up houses and shops
on Ward Road which had previously been broken into and ransacked
by soldiers who were quartered on Ward Road and the near vicinity
At 7.50.a.m. 4.12.37 three male and one female Chinese refugees
found on Singliang Road were evacuated to the south of the creek
by Police.
C. Rhodes

阁下，
1937年12月4日下午12时30分，华德路364弄发生一起原因不明的火灾，两栋中国民居被完全烧毁，另外三栋部分烧毁。日军驻扎在附近，但他们无法提供关于起火原因的任何信息。救火会到场并进行了扑救。（请参阅杂项 520/37 f.Rd.）

At 10.20.a.m. 25/11/37 a fire of unknown origin broke out among a group of country houses on Dalny Road between Nos.240 and 250 Dalny Rd, resulting in about six of the houses being totally destroyed. The cause of outbreak is not known but at the time a large number of Japanese troops were in the vicinity. The Fire Brigade attended and functioned. Owners not known as they had already evacuated. For further details please see Y'Rd Misc: Report No.475/37.
At 10/10.a.m. 25/11/37 S.P.#. No.230, Basir Khan employed at No.151 Thorburn Rd a dwelling house of Mrs. Gande, came to the station and reported that at about 9.30.a.m. 25/11/37 seventeen Japanese soldiers entered the yard and removed eight baskets of coal from a coal pile at the rear of the house. Owner informed. For further details please see Y'Rd Misc: Report No.476/37.

Misc. File No 321/37.
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
Wayside Station,
FURTHER REPORT No. 67. Date November 24, 19 37.
Subject Incidents resulting from Sino-Japanese Hostilities.
Made by D. I. Bennett. Forwarded by

Sir,
During period of patrol in Wayside District, many
Japanese soldiers, apparently not on duty, have been
observed in various parts of Wayside District, these
soldiers entering alleyways and vacant premises supposed
with the intention of searching for loot, for on several
occasions individual Japanese soldiers have been
observed in possession of small miscellaneous articles
of property which must have been looted from houses in
the alleyway in which they have been seen. (D.I. Bennett
and D. S. Sorris).

Detachments of Japanese soldiers are occupying
various premises (Chinese property) in Wayside District,
using premises as billets, storage for food and war
supplies, etc., whilst waste land on Tongshan Road near
Dalny Road is being made use of for horse lines, the
movements of troops and transport, war supplies, etc.,
being continuous passing through Wayside District, from
the various wharves in the District.

Yours obediently,

D.D.O. "D" Division.
Officer i/c Special Branch.
D.C. (Divisions).

(批：2H / 11)

主题：中日敌对行动所致事件。
呈报人：D. I. Bennett。转发人：

先生，
在路边区（Wayside District）巡逻期间，观察到许多显然非执勤状态的日本士兵出现在该区的各个角落，这些士兵进入弄堂和空置房屋，疑似意图搜寻劫掠物，因为曾数次观察到个别日本士兵持有各种零星物品，这些物品必定是从他们被看见所在的弄堂内的房屋中劫掠而来的。（D.I. Bennett 和 D. S. Sorris）。

日本军队分队正占据路边区内的多处房产（中国业主财产），将其用作营房、食品及军需物资仓库等；同时，大连路（Dalny Road）附近的通山路（Tongshan Road）上的空地正被用作马匹拴系处，部队、运输车辆及军需物资等的调动持续不断地从该区各码头穿过路边区。

此致
敬礼

“D”分区副总监。
特别科主管警官。
各分区助理总监。

Made by .................................... Forwarded by [Signature]

[Text largely illegible due to fading/damage] ... to the
office of the S.M.P. on 23/11/37 where they were dealt with
by the officer in charge of that section. The owners of the
property who were formerly employed were also notified
of their removal.

At 1.30.p.m. 23/11/37 Japanese soldiers were seen thoroughly
looting Chinese dwelling houses situated on Chemulpo Road south of
Yangtszepoo Road, several of the houses were also being used as
bill posts.

Between 2.30.p.m. and 4.00.p.m. 23/11/37 Japanese soldiers were
observed thoroughly ransacking dwelling houses on Baikal Road,
Yulin Road, and Pingliang Road.

At 2.45.p.m. 23/11/37 three Japanese soldiers entered the Chinese
owned Pioneer Knitting Factory situated at No 377 Yangtszepoo Road
and after the Russian watchman refused to open a godown for them
they broke the lock off the door and stole seven large parcels of

Sir,
At 12.25 p.m. 19/11/37 . . . 700, Charan Singh, employed
at the China American Tobacco Co., No.720 Setmore Rd came to
the station and reported that about six Japanese soldiers had
broken into the premises and after smashing open an office door
they took away his bedding and other property and then left the
premises.

At 1.05 p.m. 19/11/37 . . . 309 Smith whilst on patrol on
Chemulpo Rd noticed that the house of Mr. Hepburn, factory manager
of Messrs 'Outrie's, No.651 Chemulpo Rd had been broken into;
P.C. Smith entered the premises and on doing so he observed
two members of the Japanese Naval Landing Party run out of the
dining room through the French windows. P.C. Smith then commenced
to inspect the house when he met five Japanese soldiers coming
from the upstairs rooms. On seeing the soldiers P.C. Smith instruc-
ted J.W. .68, who was with him, to take the names of the soldiers
and the units to which they belonged, this J.W. .68 refused to do
and after passing greetings with the soldiers permitted them to
leave the house. Mr. Hepburn was communicated with and he immed-
iately attended the station and then proceeded to his house.
The "P.P." and "A.A." attended the house and found that the
premises had been searched and papers, silverware, photographs
etc had been strewn over the floors. The extent of damage done
and of property stolen is at present unknown but an estimate will
be submitted later after Mr. Hepburn has made a careful check
of the contents. For further and complete details please see
Yulin Road Misc. Report No.486/37.

At 3.30 p.m. 19/11/37 four private Indian watchmen named Sap-
uran Singh, Sidagar Singh, Bajar Singh and Boyara Singh Singh

1937 年 11 月 19 日下午 12:25，. . . 700，Charan Singh，受雇于塞莫尔路（Setmore Rd）720 号的美华烟草公司（China American Tobacco Co.），来到巡捕房报告称，约六名日本士兵闯入该处，砸开一扇办公室门后，拿走了他的寝具和其他财物，随后离开。

1937 年 11 月 19 日下午 1:05，. . . 309 Smith 警员在仁川路巡逻时，注意到仁川路 651 号 Outrie 公司工厂经理 Hepburn 先生的住宅遭人闯入；Smith 警员进入屋内，随即看到两名日本海军陆战队成员从餐厅透过法式窗户跑出去。Smith 警员随即开始检查房屋，此时遇到五名来自楼上房间的日本士兵。看到士兵后，Smith 警员指示与他在一起的 J.W. .68（警员编号）记下这些士兵的姓名及其所属部队，但 J.W. .68 拒绝执行，并在与士兵寒暄后允许他们离开房屋。随后联系了 Hepburn 先生，他立即赶到巡捕房，然后前往其住宅。“P.P.”和“A.A.”（原文缩写，可能指特定警官或部门）到达该住宅，发现屋内已被搜查，文件、银器、照片等散落在地板上。目前的损失程度和被盗财产尚不清楚，但在 Hepburn 先生仔细核对物品后将提交估算报告。更多完整详情请参阅榆林路杂项报告第 486/37 号。

1937 年 11 月 19 日下午 3:30，四名私人印度看守，名为 Sapuran Singh、Sidagar Singh、Bajar Singh 和 Boyara Singh Singh

all employed at the Sei Tung Cotton Mill, No.545 Ley Road came to

Japanese soldiers and one Japanese civilian entered the mill where
them
the Japanese civilian, speaking Chinese, asked the nationality of
the owners of the mill and on them replying that the mill was
American owned the Japanese civilian informed them that this was
not so but that the mill was Cantonese owned and in view of this
they could not remain on the premises and thereupon the Japanese
civilian and the four soldiers made them leave the premises.
Inquiries have ascertained that the Japanese military intend
to occupy the mill for about one week therefore making it imposs-
ible for the Indian watchmen to remain on the premises.
The four watchmen were duly taken South of the Creek minus
their property which they refused to remove from the mill.
Owners of the mill informed of the above.
It is worthy of note that although the entire district, with
the exception of a certain area, has been handed over to police,
it is still impossible for inquiries to be made in alleyways with-
out a member of the Japanese Naval Landing Party arriving on the
scene and ordering the police out of the alleyway. At times the
police are permitted into the alleyways but are always followed
by one or more members of the J.N.L.Party; on occasions when the
object of the visit to the alleyway becomes apparent to them they
immediately and in no uncertain terms order the police from the
alleyway. By adopting this attitude the J.N.L.Party more or less
compel the police to keep to the roadway thereby hindering the
police in their duty.

经查证，日军意图占领该工厂约一周，因此印度看守无法继续留在厂区内。
这四名看守被 duly（按规定）带往苏州河以南，未携带其财产，因为他们拒绝将财产从工厂搬出。
工厂业主已获知上述情况。
值得注意的是，尽管除特定区域外，整个辖区已移交警方管理，但若没有日本海军陆战队成员到场并将警察赶出弄堂，警方仍无法在弄堂内进行调查。有时警方被允许进入弄堂，但总会有一名或多名日本海军陆战队成员跟随；一旦他们察觉到警方进入弄堂的目的，便会立即且毫不含糊地命令警察离开弄堂。日本海军陆战队采取这种态度，或多或少迫使警察只能停留在马路上，从而阻碍了警察履行职责。

Sir,
At 9-30 a.m. 9/11/37, D.I. Bennett and D.S. Sorrie whilst
on patrol observed members of the Japanese forces (Military)
removing miscellaneous articles of clothing, beds and bedding,
from premises in Lane 894, East Seward Road.

(Military) removing miscellaneous articles of household
furniture from premises in Lane 690, East Seward Road, the

waiting in the vicinity.
Since 1/11/37, 12 refugees have been brought to Wayside
Police Station by members of the Japanese Naval Landing Party,
including 6 males who were brought to the Station on 11/11/37
from Tazang.
These males had been working for the Japanese Military
in the vicinity of Tazang, who no longer required their

employ these male Chinese, who stated that they did not wish
further employment with the Japanese due to not receiving
any pay from the Japanese Military whilst working at Tazang.
All were escorted to the Garden Bridge.

respectively, two separate fires occurred in Wayside District.

呈报人：D.S.I. McCahey。转发人：...

先生，
1937 年 11 月 9 日上午 9:30，D.I. Bennett 和 D.S. Sorrie 在巡逻时观察到日本军队（陆军）成员从东熙华德路（East Seward Road）894 弄的房屋内搬运各种衣物、床铺和被褥。
1937 年 11 月 11 日上午 9:30，D.I. Bennett 和 D.S. Sorrie 在巡逻时观察到日本军队（陆军）成员从东熙华德路 690 弄的房屋内搬运各种家用家具，这些财产被装上一辆卡车，附近还停着另外两辆卡车。
自 1937 年 11 月 1 日以来，日本海军陆战队成员已将 12 名难民带到路边巡捕房，其中包括 6 名男性，他们于 1937 年 11 月 11 日从 Tazang（音译，地名不确定）被带到巡捕房。
这些男性此前一直在 Tazang 附近为日本军队工作，因日军不再需要他们的服务，故请求上海公共租界警务处协助护送他们前往安全区。
日本海军陆战队成员希望雇用这些中国男性，但这些男性表示，由于在 Tazang 工作期间未从日本军队获得任何报酬，他们不希望再为日本人工作。
所有人均被护送至外白渡桥（Garden Bridge）。
1937 年 11 月 11 日晚间，分别在下午 6:50 和 9:24，路边区发生了两起独立的火灾。

1937年11月9日下午12时35分，巡长菲利普斯 (F.S. Phillips) 观察到日本士兵正在从位于安东路的工务局仓库搬走垃圾车。经查询得知，约在1937年11月9日下午12时30分，四五十名由一名日本平民带领的日本士兵走近在该仓库值班的印度看守人，该平民用上海话告诉看守人，他是工务局雇员/已获工务局总局许可搬走这些垃圾车。因此看守人未加反对，士兵们进入仓库并搬走垃圾车，随后推着车沿引翔港路（Y'poo Rd）向西行进。在工务局办公室进行的查询未能获得关于上述情况的任何信息。日本侦探警员149号在日本宪兵队总部进行的查询也无结果。更多详情请参阅榆林路杂项档案 434/37。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
Yulin Road Station,
REPORT
Date 9/11/37 19
Subject Theft of Municipal property by Japanese soldiers.
Made by D.S. Rhodes. Forwarded by
Sir,
At 12.35.p.m. 9/11/37 F.S. Phillips observed Japanese soldiers removing refuse barrows from the P.W.D. depot situated at Antung Road. At 2.00.p.m. Nazih Khan Police watchman employed at the above depot also reported the theft of the barrows.
Enquiries made by the undersigned ascertained that at about 12.30.p.m. 9/11/37 between forty and fifty Japanese soldiers headed by a Japanese civilian approached the watchman at the depot, and the civilian addressing the watchman in the Shanghai dialect stated that he was a P.W.D. employee and that he had been given permission from the P.W.D. Head Office to remove the barrows. The watchman therefore offered no objection and the soldiers entered the depot yard and wheeled the barrows away proceeding along Y'poo Road toward Hongkew.
Mr Barrington was communicated with and he stated that as far as he could ascertain no Japanese were employed by the P.W.D. in the Eastern area neither had they been given permission to remove the barrows.
J.D.S.149 conducted enquiries at the Japanese Military Police Headquarters with negative results.
The exact number of barrows stolen cannot be ascertained until the P.W.D. have checked same but according to the watchman the soldiers took away about forty vehicles.
Sen Det. 1/c.
D.D.O. "D".
C. [Signature]
D.S.114.

事由 日本士兵盗窃市政财产。
制作者 侦探警员罗兹 (Rhodes)。转呈者
先生，
1937年11月9日下午12时35分，巡长菲利普斯观察到日本士兵正在从位于安东路的工务局仓库搬走垃圾车。下午2时，受雇于上述仓库的警察看守人纳齐赫·汗 (Nazih Khan) 也报告了垃圾车被盗一事。
经卑职查询查明，约在1937年11月9日下午12时30分，四五十名由一名日本平民带领的日本士兵走近仓库看守人，该平民用上海话对看守人说，他是工务局雇员，并已获工务局总局许可搬走垃圾车。因此看守人未加反对，士兵们进入仓库院子，推走垃圾车，沿引翔港路向虹口方向行进。
已与巴林顿先生 (Mr Barrington) 联系，他表示据其所知，工务局在东区并未雇佣任何日本人，也未给予他们搬走垃圾车的许可。
日本侦探警员149号在日本宪兵队总部进行的查询无果。
确切被盗垃圾车数量须待工务局核查后方能确定，但据看守人称，士兵们带走了约四十辆车。
高级侦探主管。
“D”区副总监。
C. [签名]
侦探警员114号。

FURTHER REPORT No. 58. November 3, 1937
Subject Incidents resulting from Sino-Japanese Hostilities.
Made by D.S.I. McCahey. Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,
During the evening of 2/11/37, Chinese light batteries in Pootung shelled the Eastern District, the shelling being of a desultory nature, a number of shells falling in Wayside District.
Japanese men-of-war on the Whangpoo River extensively bombarded Pootung, assisted by land batteries, situation not known.
At about 10-00 a.m. on 2/11/37, Japanese troops, members of transportation companies, whilst passing through the district were observed looting shoes from a Chinese shoe shop at 45/47 Muirhead Road.
At the request of the Japanese Naval Landing Party, Japanese Police from Wayside Station have been posted at the China Merchants Lower Wharf, Broadway East, and the D.K.K. Wharf, Yangtszepoo Road, throughout the night, this being due to possible danger from outbreak of fire caused by shelling of Wayside District from Pootung, when if any such fire should occur, Japanese Naval Landing Party would know position of Police in order to request assistance.

Yours obediently,
[Signature]
D. S. I.

先生，
1937年11月2日晚间，浦东的中国轻型炮兵部队炮击东区，炮击性质零星，有多枚炮弹落在韦斯特（Wayside）辖区。
黄浦江上的日本军舰在陆地炮兵的协助下，对浦东进行了大规模轰炸，具体情况不明。
1937年11月2日上午10时许，有人观察到属于运输连队的日本 troops 在穿过辖区时，正在缪黑德路45/47号的一家中国鞋店抢劫鞋子。
应日本海军陆战队要求，来自韦斯特（Wayside）警署的日本警察整夜驻守在百老汇路（东）的招商局下栈码头以及杨树浦路的大公码头（D.K.K. Wharf），这是因为浦东对韦斯特（Wayside）辖区的炮击可能引发火灾危险，若发生此类火灾，日本海军陆战队需知晓警察的位置以便请求协助。

此致，
[签名]

Date November 6, 19 37.
Subject Incidents resulting from Sino-Japanese Hostilities.
Made by D.S.I. McCahey. Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,
During the evening of 4/11/37 and morning of 5/11/37,
members of the Japanese Naval Landing Party requested Police
assistance to interrogate four male and six female Chinese
whom they had arrested in an alleyway off Tongshan Road
between Chusan and Alcock Roads. These Chinese had in their
possession three small attache cases containing miscellaneous
articles, consisting of pens, box cameras, watches, etc.,
suspected of being loot.
When questioned, they stated that they had been living
in this vicinity since the commencement of hostilities, and
that the property was left behind by Chinese soldiers when
they retreated.
The property was entered in the Detained Property Book
and detained at this station, while the Chinese were escorted
to the Garden Bridge.
Between 9-00 a.m. and 10-00 a.m. on 5/11/37, D.I. Bennett
and Inspt. Lees whilst on patrol observed members of the
Japanese forces (Military) removing property, consisting of
miscellaneous articles of blackwood furniture, household
effects, including a gramophone and records, etc., from
premises in Lanes 31 Singkeipang Road and 235 Yuenfong Road,
the property being loaded on motor trucks.

Yours obediently,
D.D.O. "D" Division.
Officer i/c Special Branch. [Signature]

先生，
1937年11月4日晚间及11月5日上午，日本海军陆战队成员请求警方协助审讯四名男性和六名女性中国人，这些人是在舟山路与阿尔科克路之间的一条通山路上巷子里被捕的。这些中国人持有三个小公文箱，内装钢笔、盒式相机、手表等杂物，涉嫌为赃物。
受审时，他们声称自敌对行动开始以来一直居住在该附近，并称这些财产是中国士兵撤退时留下的。
该财产已登记入扣押财产簿并扣押在本警署，而这些中国人则被护送至外白渡桥。
1937年11月5日上午9时至10时之间，班尼特督察 (D.I. Bennett) 和利斯巡官 (Inspt. Lees) 在巡逻时，观察到日本军队（陆军）成员正在从辛家牌路31弄和元芳路235弄的房产中搬走财产，包括各种红木家具、家居用品（含留声机和唱片等），并将这些财产装上卡车。

Wayside Station,
FURTHER REPORT No. 57.
October 31, 37.
Subject Incidents resulting from Sino-Japanese Hostilities.
Made by D.S.I. McCahey. Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,
At 9-00 a.m. on 29/10/37, the undersigned, whilst on patrol, observed members of the Japanese Forces removing bundles of new shovels from premises off Singkeipang Road, the property being loaded on a waiting motor truck.
At 9-00 a.m. on 30/10/37, D.I. Bennett observed members of the Japanese Forces removing miscellaneous articles from premises on East Seward and Tongshan Road. The property, consisting of stoves, piping and chairs, etc., was loaded on a motor truck.
Mr. Muir, Shanghai Electric Construction Company, reported by telephone on 30/10/37 that further entry had been made into the married quarters of the Tramway Company on Yangtszepoo Road, and various articles of property stolen. Reported to British and Japanese Consular Authorities by Mr. Muir.
During the evening of 30/10/37 and early morning of 31/10/37, Chinese light batteries in Pootung shelled the Eastern District. The shelling was of a desultory nature, a number of shells falling in Wayside District, one of which is believed to be the cause of an outbreak of fire at a Japanese occupied dwelling-house in the District.
The Shanghai Fire Brigade attended and succeeded in extinguishing the fire, the dwelling-house being gutted.
Japanese men-of-war in the Whangpoo River, also Japanese land batteries, situation unknown, replied to the shelling.

Yours obediently,
[Signature]
D. S. I.

制作者 副督察麦卡希 (McCahey)。转呈者 [签名]

先生，
1937年10月29日上午9时，卑职在巡逻时，观察到日本军队成员正在从辛家牌路附近的房产中搬走成捆的新铁锹，财产被装上一辆等候的卡车。
1937年10月30日上午9时，班尼特督察 (D.I. Bennett) 观察到日本军队成员正在从东西华德路和通山路上的房产中搬走各种物品。这些财产包括炉子、管道和椅子等，被装上一辆卡车。
上海电力建设公司的缪尔先生 (Mr. Muir) 于1937年10月30日通过电话报告称，杨树浦路上的电车公司家属宿舍再次遭到闯入，各种财产被盗。缪尔先生已向英国和日本领事当局报告。
1937年10月30日晚间及10月31日凌晨，浦东的中国轻型炮兵部队炮击东区。炮击性质零星，有多枚炮弹落在韦斯特（Wayside）辖区，其中一枚被认为导致了辖区内一处被日军占用的住宅发生火灾。
上海救火会到场并成功扑灭火灾，该住宅内部被烧毁。
黄浦江上的日本军舰以及日本陆地炮兵（情况不明）进行了还击。

Sir,
During the day the district was comparitively quiet.
At 9.30.a.m. 18th S.I. Wilkinson observed Japanese soldiers removing planks of wood from a shop at No.339 Baikal Rd, owner not known.
At 10.30.a.m. 18th. Mr Cheetham (Ewo Cotton Mill) 670 Y'poo Rd telephoned to the station reporting that his house at the above address had been broken into and property stolen. Inquiries made revealed that the culprits had climbed over the wall from the Heng Fong Cotton Mill, which is next to Ewo's, by means of a ladder and had then climbed through a window of Mr Cheethams house and stole towels and knives to the value of about $200.00
As the Japanese Naval Authorities posted a notice outside the mill gates on the 15/10/37 to the effect that the property was under the protection of the J.N.L.P. the officer in command was informed and asked to have inquiries made; as Mr Cheetham does not yet know the exact amount of property stolen a complete list will be forwarded latter and a copy submitted to the J.N.L. Party.

10月18日上午10时30分，怡和纱厂（Ewo Cotton Mill）的奇塔姆先生（Mr Cheetham），住址杨树浦路670号，致电捕房报告称，其位于上述地址的住宅遭闯入，财物被盗。经查询发现，罪犯通过梯子从紧邻怡和纱厂的恒丰纱厂（Heng Fong Cotton Mill）翻墙而过，随后爬进奇塔姆先生住宅的窗户，盗走了价值约200美元的毛巾和刀具。

Made by D.S.I. McCahey. Forwarded by
Sir,
During the evening of 17/10/37 and early morning of
18/10/37, a series of air raids were carried out by the
Chinese forces, when a number of bombs were dropped in the
Eastern District, whilst from the sound of the explosions
it was thought that a number fell in Wayside District.
Damage and vicinity not ascertained.
Shrapnel from anti-aircraft guns fell in the compound
of Wayside Station.
During the evening of 17/10/37 and morning of 18/10/37,
artillery, machine gun and rifle fire was heard from the
direction of the Northern boundary of Wayside District.
On 16/10/37 Mr. L.H. Richards, (British) employed at
Liddel Brothers and Company, 284 Yangtsepoo Road, where he
was formerly residing in a flat situated on top of one of
above company's godowns, reported to Inspector Bennett the
forcible entry and looting of his flat since the commencement
of hostilities on 14/8/37, when he evacuated these premises.
This flat was visited on or about 9/10/37, when it was
found to have been forcibly entered and ransacked, but on
the 16/10/37, upon being visited again it showed signs of
further entry, forcible opening of drawers and rooms, which
had been ransacked, and food and drinks consumed upon the
premises, whilst property, amount not known, had been taken away.
Mr. Richards stated that he would report the incident to
British Consular Authorities.
Condition of flat on 16/10/37 corroborated by D.I. Bennett.
During the period in the early weeks of October 1937,
Japanese troops (military) were making use of the area in

在1937年10月17日晚及10月18日凌晨，中国军队发动了一系列空袭，多枚炸弹落入东区，同时根据爆炸声判断，认为有多枚炸弹落入韦赛德区。
损害情况及具体地点尚未查明。
高射炮的弹片落入韦赛德捕房的大院内。
在1937年10月17日晚及10月18日上午，听到来自韦赛德区北界方向传来火炮、机枪和步枪射击声。
1937年10月16日，受雇于杨树浦路284号利德尔兄弟公司（Liddel Brothers and Company）的英国人 L.H. 理查兹先生报告贝内特督察，自1937年8月14日敌对行动开始他撤离该处以来，其住所遭到强行闯入和抢劫。他此前居住在该公司一座仓库顶部的公寓内。
该公寓于10月9日左右曾去查看，当时发现已被强行闯入并洗劫，但在10月16日再次查看时，显示出进一步闯入的迹象，抽屉和房间被强行打开并遭洗劫，现场的食物和饮料被消耗，同时有财产被带走，数量不详。
理查兹先生表示，他将向英国领事当局报告此事。
侦探员贝内特证实了10月16日公寓的状况。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
Wayside
FURTHER REPORT No. 46.
Date October 16, 1937.
Subject Incidents resulting from Sino-Japanese Hostilities.
Made by D.S.I. McCahey. Forwarded by
Sir,
At about 5-30 p.m. on 14/10/37, extensive shelling
from Chinese light artillery, apparently from Pootung and
Chapel, took place. The bombardment was continued for
nearly one hour, many shells falling in Wayside District.
During this bombardment, a series of air raids were
carried out by the Chinese forces, bombs being dropped in
the Eastern District. Other air raids took place during
the late evening of 14/10/37 and early morning of 15/10/37,
no bombs as far as can be ascertained falling in Wayside
District.
Shrapnel from anti-aircraft guns fell in the compound
of Wayside Station.
Damage noted by Shells:-
One struck premises, 131 Yangtsepoo Road, a Chinese
dwelling-house, causing damage to upper floor.
Two struck premises on the Shanghai and Hongkew Wharf,
causing very trivial damage.
Foreign dwelling-houses, 2, 4, 20, 26 and 30 Studley
Avenue, (Baikal Road) were each struck by a shell, causing
trivial damage to brickwork and windows of these premises.
Premises at 87/89 Baikal Road, a Chinese dwelling-house,
were also damaged by a shell which struck the pavement.
One shell struck the skeleton wall of a godown of the
Nanyang Brothers Tobacco Company, Chaoufoong Road.
During the morning of 15/10/37, Japanese warships on
the Whangpoo River opened fire in the Pootung direction with
machine guns.
At 9-00 a.m. on 14/10/37, Inspector Bennett observed a

第 46 号补充报告。
日期：1937年10月16日。
主题：中日敌对行动所致事件。
呈报人：副督察长麦卡希（McCahey）。转呈人：
敬启者，
1937年10月14日下午5时30分左右，发生大规模炮击，据信来自中国轻型火炮，发射地点似乎为浦东和 Chapel（音译）。轰炸持续了近一个小时，许多炮弹落在韦斯特区（Wayside District）。
在此次轰炸期间，中国军队实施了一系列空袭，炸弹投掷在东区。1937年10月14日深夜及10月15日凌晨又发生了其他空袭，据查无炸弹落在韦斯特区。
高射炮的弹片落在韦斯特警署大院内。
炮弹造成的损坏如下：
一枚击中杨树浦路131号 premises（一处华人住宅），导致二楼受损。
两枚击中上海与虹口码头（Shanghai and Hongkew Wharf）上的建筑物，造成极轻微损坏。
司徒雷登路（Studley Avenue，即贝加尔路 Baikal Road）2号、4号、20号、26号和30号的外侨住宅各被一枚炮弹击中，造成这些建筑物的砖墙和窗户轻微受损。
贝加尔路87/89号的 premises（一处华人住宅）也被一枚击中人行道的炮弹损坏。
一枚炮弹击中了兆丰路（Chaoufoong Road）南洋兄弟烟草公司仓库的骨架墙。
1937年10月15日上午，黄浦江上的日本军舰向浦东方向开火射击机枪。

Yangtsepoo
18th October 37.
Sino-Japanese hostilities in the Yangtsepoo district for 24 hours
ending 6 a.m. 18/10/37.
D.S.I.Crighton.
Officer i/c.

Sir,
I beg to report that as result of investigations made
on the morning of the 17/10/37, it was ascertained that three
of the numerous bombs dropped during the Chinese air raids
on the night of the 16/10/37, fell in the vacant ground adjoin-
ing the Japanese Commercial School, Pingliang road, 100 yards
east of this station.
Throughout the morning and afternoon of the 16/10/37,
other than for occasional bombardments by Japanese men-o-war
lying in the river of Pootung and Chapel areas nothing of an
outstanding nature took place.
At 7 p.m. 16/10/37 Chinese bombing planes flew over this
district, dropping incendiary bombs at the following places;-
1st. Into a coal dump, located inside the compound of the Asi
Steel Factory, a Japanese concern located at 379 Hochien road
causing practically no damage. 2nd. On a piece of vacant
ground, 10 yards behind the No.1 Daiichi Soap Factory, a Japa-
nese concern, located at 479 Hochien road, causing no damage.
3rd. On to a two storey building, located at the south east
corner of the Seventh Day Adventist Mission compound, an
American concern, situated at 525 Ningkou road, completely
gutted by fire. These premises are thought to be used as eit-
quarters for chineses staff, or school rooms, but nothing defi-
can be ascertained. 4th. two bombs dropped into the vacant
ground just west of Kwangshing road, property of the China
Import and Export Co. but no damage done.
Reference to fire at the Seventh Day adventist miss-

be summoned to extinguished same. This was done, J.D.S.42 an

1937年10月18日。
截至1937年10月18日上午6时的24小时内，杨树浦地区的中日敌对行动情况。
副督察长克里顿（Crighton）。
主管警官。

敬启者，
谨报告，经1937年10月17日上午调查查明，1937年10月16日夜中国空军空袭期间投下的众多炸弹中，有三枚落在我站以东100码、平凉路日本商业学校旁的空地上。
1937年10月16日整个上午和下午，除了停泊在河面上的日本军舰偶尔炮击浦东和 Chapel（音译）地区外，未发生其他显著事件。
1937年10月16日晚7时，中国轰炸机飞越本区，在以下地点投掷燃烧弹：
1. 投入和兴路379号亚细亚钢铁厂（Asi Steel Factory，一家日商企业）大院内的煤堆，几乎未造成损坏。
2. 投在和兴路479号第一制皂厂（Daiichi Soap Factory No.1，一家日商企业）后方10码的一块空地上，未造成损坏。
3. 投在宁国路525号基督复临安息日会传教团（Seventh Day Adventist Mission，一家美资机构）大院东南角的一栋两层建筑上，该建筑被大火完全烧毁。这些 premises 被认为用作华人员工宿舍或教室，但无法确证。
4. 两枚炸弹投在广生行路（Kwangshing road）以西的空地上，该地为中国进出口公司（China Import and Export Co.）产业，但未造成损坏。
关于基督复临安息日会传教团火灾一事，
日本海军陆战队（J.N.L.P.）来到警署，要求召唤消防队灭火。随即照办，由日本驱逐舰42号（J.D.S.42）及

the undersigned providing the necessary escort,and after one
hour the fire was completely extinguished.It is worthy of not
that on arrival of police and fire brigade,the J.N.L.P. were
already functioning with fire appliances obtained from the
Tung Hwa Cotton Mill,a Japanese concern located on Ward Road.
At 10-20 p.m. 17/10/37,Chinese planes again flew over
this district,dropping two incendiary bombs in the vicinity
of Yangtzepoo road,exact location at present unknown.
At the following times,12-37 to 1-5 a.m. ,1-53 to 2-5
a.m,and 2-15 to 2-45 a.m. 18/10/37,Chinese bombing planes raided
this area,dropping numerous bombs in and around this district
exact location at present unknown.
During the foregoing raids,Japanese anti-aircraft
was very prominent,several pieces of shrapnel falling in the
vicinity of this station. No casualties reported,and as far
as can be ascertained no planes brought down.
In conclusion,I beg to report,that at 12-15 p.m. 17/1

本人提供必要护卫，一小时后大火被完全扑灭。值得注意的是，警察和消防队到达时，日本海军陆战队已经在使用从通华纱厂（Tung Hwa Cotton Mill，一家位于华德路的日商企业）获得的消防设备进行灭火作业。
1937年10月17日晚10时20分，中国飞机再次飞越本区，在杨树浦路附近投下两枚燃烧弹，确切位置目前不详。
在以下时间段：1937年10月18日凌晨12时37分至1时05分、1时53分至2时05分，以及2时15分至2时45分，中国轰炸机空袭该地区，在本区及周边投下大量炸弹，确切位置目前不详。
在上述空袭期间，日本高射炮活动非常频繁，几块弹片落在我站附近。据报无人员伤亡，据查亦无飞机被击落。
最后，谨报告，1937年10月17日中午12时15分，受雇于首尔路140号永安纱厂（Wing On Cotton Mills）的私人守夜人萨哈姆·辛格（Saham Singh）来到警署报告称，1937年10月13日，三辆日本海军陆战队（J.N.L.P.）摩托卡车前往该厂运走了三车棉布。1937年10月14日，十一辆类似的卡车也做了同样的事，1937年10月16日，一辆卡车运走了一车椅子、桌子、凳子等物品。

Yangtsepoo
19th October 37.

Sino-Japanese hostilities in Yangtsepoo district for 24 hours
ending 6 a.m. 19/10/37.
D.S.I.Crighton.                                      (Signature) Officer i/c.

Sir,
    I beg to report that throughout the past twenty four hours
other for occasional firing of guns from the river, and bomb-
ing of Pootung area by Japanese planes, hostilities have been
on the whole quiet, in this district.
    At 11 a.m. 18/10/37 a telephone message was received
from C.J. Capt. Grubb D.D.O. "D", reporting that whilst driving
along Yangtsepoo road, he had observed several M/trucks
driven by Japanese military, load up with cotton leaving the
Wing On Company Godowns 1616 Yangtsepoo road.
    At 2-20 p.m. 18/10/37, a fire was observed at Yangtsepoo
and Weinan roads corner. The S.F.B. were summoned, and after
one hour succeeded in extinguishing same. For full particulars
See Fire Report No. 219/37 as submitted by D.S. Duke.
    Reference to the bombing on the night of 17/10/37,
further enquires revealed that a bomb had been dropped into
a chinese shop at 1656 Yangtsepoo road, completely demolishing
same.

                                                I am, Sir,

1937年10月19日。

截至1937年10月19日上午6时的24小时内，杨树浦地区的中日敌对行动情况。
副督察长克里顿（Crighton）。                                      （签名）主管警官。

敬启者，
    谨报告，在过去二十四小时内，除了来自河面的偶尔炮击以及日本飞机对浦东地区的轰炸外，本区的敌对行动总体平静。
    1937年10月18日上午11时，接到“D”分区副分区指挥官格鲁布（Grubb）上尉的电话留言，报告称他在沿杨树浦路行驶时，观察到几辆由日军驾驶的摩托卡车装载着棉花离开位于杨树浦路1616号的永安公司仓库。
    1937年10月18日下午2时20分，观察到杨树浦路与渭南路口发生火灾。召唤上海消防队（S.F.B.），经过一小时成功将火扑灭。详情参见杜克（Duke）副督察提交的第 219/37 号火灾报告。

Yangtsepoo
20th October 37
Sino Japanese hostilities in the Yangtsepoo district for 24
Hours ending 6 a.m. 20/10/37.
D.S.Muke. [Signature] Officer i/c.

Sir,

I beg to report that conditions on both sides in this
vicinity appeared to be uneventful until 1.15 a.m. when a
Chinese plane appeared with great stealth and flew rapidly
over the district, little anti-air craft fire being directed
against it. The plane was seen to drop five bombs, thought to
be incendiary, in quick succession west of the station. No
fires were observed as a consequence and no reports of hits
have yet been received. From brief enquiries in the district
this morning it is thought that some of these bombs fell in
the compound of the Wing On No.1 mill, Seoul Rd., occupied by
Japanese troops, and the remainder on vacant land to the North

At 2.20 p.m. private watchman, Harjana Singh, reported
that at at 8 a.m. and 4 p.m. 18/10/37 Japanese soldiers
removed 6 trucks of raw cotton from the Wing On No.1 Cotton
mill, 140 Seoul road.

It was discovered yesterday that at some time during
shelling on 17/10/37, or possibly during the air-raid, further
damage was done to the Orient Paint Co. What appears to be
either a small shell or anti-air craft fragments has penetrated
the glass roof of a paint godown situated on the North side
of the main gate on Tengyueh Rd., causing damage to wire
shelves and paint stored in small tins.

I am, Sir,
yours obediently

穆克（Muke）副督察。[签名] 主管警官。

敬启者，

谨报告，本地区双方局势一直平淡无奇，直到凌晨1时15分，一架中国飞机悄然出现并迅速飞越该区，针对它的高射炮火很少。只见该飞机在警署西侧快速连续投下五枚炸弹，推测为燃烧弹。未见因此引发火灾，也未收到命中报告。今早在本区简要查询后，认为其中一些炸弹落在被日军占领的首尔路永安一厂（Wing On No.1 mill）大院内，其余落在北面的空地上。

下午2时20分，私人守夜人哈尔贾纳·辛格（Harjana Singh）报告称，1937年10月18日上午8时和下午4时，日本士兵从首尔路140号永安一厂运走了6卡车原棉。

昨日发现，在1937年10月17日的炮击期间，或者可能在空袭期间，东方油漆公司（Orient Paint Co.）遭受了进一步损坏。看似是一枚小炮弹或高射炮碎片穿透了位于腾越路（Tengyueh Rd.）大门北侧的一个油漆仓库的玻璃屋顶，导致铁丝货架和储存在小罐中的油漆受损。

此致

13th October 37.

Sino-Japanese hostilities in the Yangtzepoo district for 24
hours ending 6 a.m. 14/10/37.
D.S.I.Crighton.                                  (签名) Officer i/c.

Sir,
    I beg to report that throughout the morning and afternoon
of 13/10/37, Japanese men-o-war and air force continued to
bombard the Pootung area, directly opposite to this district.
    Between 10 a.m. and 12 Noon, J.D.S.42 accompanied by the
undersigned, after obtaining permission from the officer i/c.
of No.1 company J.N.L.F., patrolled this district North of
Pingliang road, and as a result ascertained that severe dam-
age has been done to all properties on the North side of Ward
road, practically all houses, shops, etc, being completely demo-
lished. On the south side of Ward road, commencing at Ley road
bridge and proceeding east, the following properties have been
damaged;- Sung Sing No.5 Cotton Mill completely gutted by
fire, Shanghai Printing and Dying Factory, partly damaged by
shell fire, premises have been entered and ransacked, Kofa
Drug Company, premises entered and ransacked, also slightly
damaged by fire; Zung Tuh Cotton Mill partly gutted by fire.
In addition to aforegoing the whole of Ying Ziang Kong Vill-
age has been gutted by fire. Other firms of note effected
in that area, include China Aluminium Rolling Mills Meichow
Road, Sung Sing No.6 Cotton Mill, Seoul road, Sien Dah Machine
Works, Hoochien road. Mei Hwa Printing and Dying Factory,
Hochien road. Temporary permission has now been granted the
undersigned and J.D.S.42 to patrol this area at any time.
    At 3-15 p.m. 13/10/37, private Indian watchman Sehan
Singh, employed at the Wing On Company godowns, 1516 Yangtze-
poo road, came to station and reported that between 2 and 3 p.
m. 12/10/37, and again to-day at approximately the same time,
Japanese military had entered the premises and removed four

副督察长克里顿（Crighton）。                                  （签名）主管警官。

敬启者，
    谨报告，1937年10月13日整个上午和下午，日本军舰和空军继续轰炸与本区正对的浦东地区。
    上午10时至中午12时之间，日本驱逐舰42号（J.D.S.42）在获得日本海军陆战队第一连主管警官许可后，由本人陪同，巡逻了平凉路以北的本区，结果查明华德路（Ward road）北侧的所有财产均遭受严重破坏，几乎所有房屋、商店等均被完全摧毁。在华德路南侧，从雷路（Ley road）桥开始向东，以下财产受损：申新五厂（Sung Sing No.5 Cotton Mill）被大火完全烧毁；上海印染厂（Shanghai Printing and Dying Factory）部分被炮火损坏，premises 被闯入并洗劫；科发药房（Kofa Drug Company），premises 被闯入并洗劫，亦受轻微火灾损坏；中和纱厂（Zung Tuh Cotton Mill）部分被烧毁。此外，整个英祥公村（Ying Ziang Kong Village）被大火烧毁。该地区受影响的其他著名商号包括：美周路（Meichow Road）的中国铝轧钢厂（China Aluminium Rolling Mills）、首尔路的申新六厂（Sung Sing No.6 Cotton Mill）、和兴路的先达机器厂（Sien Dah Machine Works）、和兴路的梅花印染厂（Mei Hwa Printing and Dying Factory）。现已授予本人和日本驱逐舰42号随时巡逻该区域的临时许可。

FURTHER REPORT No. 45.
Date October 14, 19 37.
Subject Incidents resulting from Sino-Japanese Hostilities.
Made by D.S.I. McCahey. Forwarded by
Sir,
On the 11th. and 12th. October, ten Chinese refugees were evacuated by the Japanese Naval Landing Party from vicinity of Jansen, Ward and Kungping Roads. These were escorted over the Garden Bridge by S.M. Police.
During the late evening of 13th. and early morning of 14th. October, intermittent rifle and machine gun fire was heard from the direction of the Northern Boundary of Wayside District. Other explosions, probably hand grenades or trench mortars, were also heard.
At 3-45 p.m. 13th. October, Inspector Lees and D.S. Sorrie on patrol, observed members of the J.N.L. Party removing steel plates from premises 396 Kungping Road, "Union Commercial Belge de Metallurgie" (Belgian) which were loaded on to a motor truck.
Three other trucks were waiting in the vicinity, probably for same purpose.
(A letter requesting protection was received from this company on 12/10/37. F2900/422.)
At about 3 p.m. 13/10/37, D.I. Bennett whilst on patrol observed papers falling from a Japanese aeroplane which was flying overhead.
One of these papers was found and ascertained to be the "Sin Shun Pao" dated 13/10/37, printed in Chinese by the Japanese press, which, from its contents are evidently Japanese propaganda.
(Newspaper forwarded to Special Branch H.Q.)
Yours obediently,
D.D.O. "D" Division.
Officer i/c Special Branch.
D. S. I.

日期：1937年10月14日。
主题：中日敌对行动所致事件。
呈报人：副督察长麦卡希（McCahey）。转呈人：
敬启者，
10月11日和12日，十名中国难民被日本海军陆战队从詹森路（Jansen）、华德路（Ward）和公平路（Kungping）附近疏散。这些人由上海公共租界警察护送至外白渡桥。
10月13日深夜及10月14日凌晨，听到来自韦斯特区北界方向传来间歇性的步枪和机枪声。还听到其他爆炸声，可能是手榴弹或战壕迫击炮。
10月13日下午3时45分，利斯（Lees）巡官和索里（Sorrie）副督察在巡逻时，观察到日本海军陆战队（J.N.L. Party）成员正在从公平路396号 premises “比利时联合冶金商业公司”（Union Commercial Belge de Metallurgie，比利时）拆除钢板，并将其装上一辆摩托卡车。
另有三辆卡车在附近等候，可能也是出于同样目的。
（该公司于1937年10月12日收到一封请求保护的信件。F2900/422。）
1937年10月13日下午3点左右，班尼特（Bennett）副督察在巡逻时观察到纸张从头顶飞过的日本飞机上落下。
找到其中一张纸，确认为1937年10月13日的《新顺报》（Sin Shun Pao），由日本报社用中文印刷，从其内容来看，显然是日本宣传品。
（报纸已转送特别分部总部。）
此致

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No...
S.I, Special Branch
REPORT
Date October 13, 19 37.
Subject Foreign houses on Baikal Road used as stables.
Made by D.S. Hocking Forwarded by
Referring to the attached news clipping of October 11,
enquiries instituted at Wayside and Yulin Road Stations reveal
that such an assertion cannot be based on fact. With few
exceptions, that section of Baikal Road which runs through
Yulin Road District (Dalny Road to Lay Road), has no foreign
houses, and in these exceptions the houses are so far unoccupied
by troops. In Wayside District, not only Baikal Road but all
that sector enclosed by Yangtzepoo Road, Dalny Road, Ward Road
and Muirhead Road is being utilized by Japanese troops, including
cavalry units with some thousands of horses, as billets.
The roadways, pavements, gardens and all available free space
has been commandeered for quartering both men and horses.
A close inspection of the houses in this area is obviously
impossible at the present time as this area is in the prohibited
zone.
D.S. Hocking
D. S.
D.C. (Special Branch).
（印：B 13 OCT 1937）

参照附件中10月11日的新闻剪报，经在韦斯特路（Wayside）站和榆林路站进行的查询显示，此类说法缺乏事实依据。除少数例外，穿过榆林路辖区（大连路至雷路）的那段贝加尔路上并没有外国房屋，而在这些例外情况下，房屋也尚未被军队占用。在韦斯特路辖区，不仅贝加尔路，而且由杨树浦路、大连路、华德路和缪尔黑德路所包围的整个区域，正被日军（包括拥有数千匹马的骑兵部队）用作营房。道路、人行道、花园及所有可用的空地均被征用，用于安置人员和马匹。
鉴于该区域处于禁区范围内，目前显然无法对该区域内的房屋进行近距离检查。

Baikal Road Foreign
Houses Now Stables

A number of houses in Baikal
Road in which British and other
foreigners resided have been
turned into stables by the Japan-
ese troops there being horses in

adjoining houses, the latter named persons however remained down-
stairs where they were found by the Japanese. Van Foh Pao states
that he heard the Japanese ask the two old women if there were
any other people in the house and if they had any money, and when
the women replied in the negative to both questions the Japanese
searched the downstairs rooms and just before leaving they ran
the two old women through with their bayonets. When the other
occupants descended they found the old women lying on the floor
bleeding from their wounds in the chest; that same day the old
women died and since then until found by police on the 3/10/37
the above refugees have been living in the house with the bodies.
The two bodies are in a very decomposed condition and smell terri-
bly. In the adjoining house (No.16) the bones of another person
were found, the identity of these remains are unknown to the
refugees. The refugees further added that whilst the Japanese
soldiers were in the alley they bayoneted about six other persons
unknown to them; no trace of these latter persons could be found, ,
in view of this a house to house search of this alley will be
made in an effort to trace these persons.
At 11.a.m 3/10/37 one Mit Singh, Indian watchman employed
at Woodworths Engineering factory at No.60 Tanyang Rd reported
