3rd October 37.

Sino-Japanese hostilities in Yangtszepoo district for 24 hours
ending 6 a.m. 3/10/37.
D.S.I.Crighton.                                  Alexander officer i/c.

Sir,
    I beg to report throughout the morning and afternoon of
the 2/10/37 Japanese men-o-war lying in the river continued
to bombard the Kiangwan area, also Japanese bombing planes
made repeated raids on the same sector, i.e. between Civic
Centre and Kiangwan Race course.
    At 150 p.m. 2/10/37, Mahander Singh, Indian private watch-
man, employed and residing at the Oriental Paint Factory,
a British concern owned by Butterfield & Swire Co., located at
2200 Pingliang road, came to station and reported that during
his temporary absence from these premises, between afternoon of
the 29/9/37 and 1-15 p.m. 2/10/37, the house of Mr. Rodger work
manager had been broken into, and the contents of two cases,
mostly silverware and curio's looted. Further the offices
had been similarly treated, but whether or not anything had
been stolen he could not say. He further reported that on his
return at 1-15 p.m., whilst standing at Yangtszepoo station
gate talking to one of the S.P.C.s on duty he observed two
plain clothes Japanese, come from the direction of Mr. Rodgers
home carrying a bundle, and enter the Japanese Commercial
School, next door to this station, and that this roused his
suspicions. As this property is within the "Prohibited Area"
informant was instructed to return to the home of Mr. Rodger and
that the police would call there after gaining the necessary
assistance. No sooner had the Indian left than he returned
carrying two curio's, stating that on entering the house on
this occasion he found two plain clothes Japanese therein
packing other property belonging to Mr. Rodger. Both Japanese
seeing him absconded, and were seen to enter the Japanese

截至1937年10月3日上午6时的24小时内，杨树浦辖区的中日敌对行动。
D.S.I Crighton。                                  Alexander 主管警官。

先生，
    谨报告，1937年10月2日整个上午和下午，停泊在江面上的日本军舰持续炮击江湾地区，日本轰炸机也对同一区域，即市中心与江湾赛马场之间，进行了多次空袭。
    1937年10月2日下午1时50分，受雇并居住在平凉路2200号东方油漆厂（英商，怡和洋行旗下）的印度私人看守 Mahander Singh 来到警局报告称，在他于1937年9月29日下午至1937年10月2日下午1时15分期间暂时离开该处时，经理 Rodger 先生的住宅遭到闯入，两只箱子的内容物，主要是银器和古玩，被抢劫。此外，办公室也遭到同样对待，但他无法确定是否有物品被盗。他还报告称，他在下午1时15分返回时，站在杨树浦站门口与一名值班的特别警察交谈，观察到两名便衣日本人从 Rodger 先生家的方向走来，携带一个包裹，进入与本站相邻的日本商业学校，这引起了他的怀疑。由于该物业位于“禁区”内，线人被指示返回 Rodger 先生家中，警方将在获得必要协助后前往该处。这名印度人刚离开就回来了，手里拿着两件古玩，声称这次进入房子时，发现里面有两名便衣日本人正在打包属于 Rodger 先生的其他财产。两名日本人看到他后逃跑了，并被看到进入日本

The aforegoing was reported to Supt.Sugi-
and his assistance requested in trying to at least recover
the property,and with this end in view he accompanied by
J.D.S.42 visited the aforesaid school,which has lately been

had arrested three members of his staff,a cook,and two

and that he was handing them over to the Military Police

he had also recovered. The property he stated would be re-

At 9-30 p.m. 2/10/37 Chinese bombing
planes again visited this district,and after flying direct-
ly over the station in a North east direction was heard to
drop five bombs,the first of which appeared to be just at
the rear of the station,whilst the others seemed to drop

FURTHER REPORT No. 32. Date Sept. 25th, 1937.
Subject Incidents resulting from Sino-Japanese Hostilities.
Made by D.S.I. McCahoy. Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,
At 6-45 p.m. Sept. 24th. a Japanese Marine Patrol called
at Wayside Station and reported lights showing on the fourth
floor of the Imperial Chemical Industries, 701 East Seward Road,
and requested assistance to have them extinguished. D.I. Bennett,
Officer i/c, the undersigned, and J.P.C. 206 attended.
An Indian Watchman was found on the premises, but not in
possession of keys to the godown concerned.
The Watchman stated he would open the Chaoufoong Road
gate and on the way police discovered that another party of
Marines had already broken the front door of 215 Chaoufoong
Road, property also belonging to the I.C.I. On being questioned
these men alleged that a light was shown on the top floor.
This light was not seen by police on the way down East
Seward Road from Station some minutes before, therefore
it is suspected the party were in the house longer than
necessary.
The Patrol were informed that the premises were British
property and that police could not assist in breaking locks.
After persuasion Patrol agreed to police telephoning the
Manager Mr. Bishop to fetch the keys and that he would be
met at the Garden Bridge. This was agreed to and at 7-45 p.m.
Mr. Bishop and Mr. Perry of I.C.I. were met by two Marines,
J.P.C. 206 and the undersigned. An escort was provided by
the Garden Bridge Guard for the return trip of the I.C.I. party.
At 8 p.m. the lights were extinguished by knocking out
of main switch.
Police returned to Station at 8-15 p.m.
It has been ascertained that the S.P. Co. were doing

由副督察长麦卡霍伊（D.S.I. McCahoy）呈报。转发人 [签名]

先生，
1937年9月24日下午6点45分，一支日本海军陆战队巡逻队来到路边巡捕房，报告称西华德路（East Seward Road）701号帝国化学工业公司（Imperial Chemical Industries）四楼有灯光显示，并请求协助将其熄灭。负责警官贝内特督察（D.I. Bennett）、本人及印籍警员第206号（J.P.C. 206）前往处理。
在现场发现一名印度看守人，但他没有相关仓库的钥匙。
看守人称他将打开兆丰路（Chaoufoong Road）的大门，途中警方发现另一队海军陆战队员已经破坏了兆丰路215号的前门，该房产也属于帝国化学工业公司。经询问，这些人声称顶层有灯光显示。
几分钟前，警方从巡捕房沿西华德路下行时并未看到此灯光，因此怀疑这队人员在屋内停留的时间超过了必要限度。
巡逻队被告知该处为英国财产，警方不能协助撬锁。经劝说，巡逻队同意由警方致电经理毕晓普先生（Mr. Bishop）取来钥匙，并将在外白渡桥（Garden Bridge）与其会合。双方达成一致，下午7点45分，两名海军陆战队员、印籍警员第206号及本人在外白渡桥会见了帝国化学工业公司的毕晓普先生和佩里先生（Mr. Perry）。外白渡桥守卫队为帝国化学工业公司人员的返程提供了护卫。
晚上8点，通过切断主开关熄灭了灯光。
警方于晚上8点15分返回巡捕房。
经查实，S.P.公司当时正在

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
Wayside Station,
Further REPORT No. 36.
Date. Sept. 28th. 1937.
Subject Incidents resulting from Sino-Japanese Hostilities.
Made by D.S.I. McCahey. Forwarded by
Sir,
At 4-30 p.m. Sept. 27th. Japanese Marines brought to
this station from the vicinity of Ward-Kinchow Roads twenty
Chinese refugees. Kept overnight, these together with eleven
others brought to station from Kashing Road District were
escorted over the Garden Bridge at 3-30 p.m. Sept. 28th.
Many firms and families took advantage of notification
in Newspapers on Sunday morning Sept. 26th. to remove goods
and personal property on 26th. and 27th. All available
members of Japanese S.M.P. at Wayside Station being utilized
to act as escorts in the district throughout the two days.
At 5 a.m. Sept. 29th. a shell exploded in vicinity of
Wayside Station and was followed by several others which
passed over the station and exploded on North side. They
were believed to have been fired from Pootung and were
immediately replied to by heavy salvos from Japanese Naval
guns in Whangpoo. Firing lasted for about thirty minutes.
All roads South of Tongshan Road were patrolled by the
undersigned after 6 a.m. by no trace of these Chinese shells
could be found.
During this patrol two motor trucks and one saloon car
were observed ranked on Kungping Road north of Tongshan Road
and several Japanese marines and Ronin forcing entry to the
many second-hand shops still intact in that road. These
vehicles were later seen entering the China Merchants Lower
Wharf premises which are occupied by J.N.L. Party.
Yours obediently,
D.D.C. "D" Division.
Officer i/c Special Branch.
D.C. (Divisions).

日期：1937年9月28日。
主题：中日敌对行动所致事件。
由副督察长麦卡希（D.S.I. McCahey）呈报。转发人
先生，
1937年9月27日下午4点30分，日本海军陆战队将二十名中国难民从华德路与荆州路（Ward-Kinchow Roads）附近带至本巡捕房。这些难民过夜后，连同从嘉兴路（Kashing Road）区带至巡捕房的另外十一人，于1937年9月28日下午3点30分在外白渡桥护送过桥。
许多商号和家庭利用了9月26日（星期日）上午报纸上的通知，于26日和27日搬运货物和个人财产。路边巡捕房所有可用的日籍上海公共租界工部局警务处（Japanese S.M.P.）成员在这两天内均被用作区内的护送人员。
1937年9月29日凌晨5点，一枚炮弹在路边巡捕房附近爆炸，随后又有数枚炮弹飞过巡捕房并在北侧爆炸。据信这些炮弹是从浦东（Pootung）发射的，黄浦江上的日本海军舰炮立即以猛烈的齐射予以回击。炮击持续了约三十分钟。
上午6点后，本人巡逻了通山路（Tongshan Road）以南的所有道路，但未发现这些中国炮弹的任何踪迹。
在巡逻期间，观察到两辆卡车和一辆轿车停在通山路以北的公平路（Kungping Road）上，几名日本海军陆战队员和浪人（Ronin）正在强行进入该路上许多仍完好无损的旧货店。后来看到这些车辆进入了由中国轮船公司下栈（China Merchants Lower Wharf）的场所，该处由日本海军陆战队（J.N.L. Party）占据。

Subject Incidents resulting from Sino-Japanese Hostilities.
Made by D.S.I. McChey. Forwarded by
Sir,
During the 23rd., 24th. and 25th. Sept., members of the
Public Health Dept., assisted by S.M. Police, have burnt the
bodies of 92 Chinese soldiers found in various roads and
houses in Wayside District north of Tongshan Road area,
whilst during this period 240 hand grenades, shell and other
explosives, and a large quantity of small arms ammunition,
have been collected from various roads and buildings and
deposited in the Whangpoo River, the assistance of members
of the Japanese Naval Landing Party being of invaluable
help during the collection and disposal of these explosives.
At 9-10 a.m. on Sept. 26th., D.I. Bennett whilst on
patrol observed members of the Japanese Naval Landing Party
loading a motor truck with trunks, which they were taking
from a Chinese shop at 832 East Seward Road.
During the twenty-four hours ending 7 a.m. on Sept. 27th,
Wayside District remained quiet.
Yours obediently,
D. S. I.

先生，
在9月23日、24日和25日期间，公共卫生局成员在上海公共租界工部局警务处的协助下，焚烧了在通山路以北的路边区各条道路和房屋中发现的92具中国士兵尸体；在此期间，从各条道路和建筑物中收集了240枚手榴弹、炮弹和其他爆炸物，以及大量轻武器弹药，并将其投入黄浦江，日本海军陆战队成员在收集和处置这些爆炸物期间提供了 invaluable 的帮助。
9月26日上午9点10分，贝内特督察（D.I. Bennett）在巡逻时观察到日本海军陆战队成员正在将行李箱装上一辆卡车，这些箱子是他们从西华德路835号的一家中国商店里拿出来的。

27th Sept. 37.

Municipal property removed by Japanese military authorities.

D. S. I. Crighton          (Signature) Officer i/c.

Sir,

    I beg to report that on the morning of the 26/9/37, it was
discovered that one of three road rollers, the property of P.W.D
S.M.C, left on Yangtsepoo road outside the China Soap Company
at the outbreak of the present hostilities had been taken away,
whilst another had been left standing on the crown of the road
causing a serious obstruction to traffic. Subsequent enquires
revealed that at approximately 12 M.N. 25/9/37, the engines of
these three road rollers were heard to start by R.P.W.138 employ-
ed at the China Soap Co, and he on peering through between the
main gate and its cement support, noticed the smallest of the three
rollers being driven away in an easterly direction by Japanese
in uniform, whether J.N.L.P. or Military cannot be definitely
stated. Similiar attempts were in the meantime being made by
other members of the party to remove the other two, but after
getting the largest one onto the crown of the road where it
stalled, the party abandoned them. At 11-30 a.m. 26/9/37 J.D.S.42
visited the J.N.L.P. Headquarters Pingliang road, where he reported
the aforegoing to Capt. Noguchi, who in reply stated that this
roller had probably been taken to the Japanese airdrome by the
military authorities as he had issued no instructions regarding
its removal. He further stated that if such was the case the
property would be well looked after, and returned to its original
position later. At 6 a.m. 27/9/37, whilst on patrol, it was discov-
ed that the remaining two rollers had also been removed, enquires
disclosing that they had been removed under their own power at
daylight this a.m. by Japanese military authorities, and taken
east along Yangtsepoo road.

(Signature)
27/9

1937年9月27日。

日本军方当局移走的市政财产。

副督察长克里顿（D. S. I. Crighton）          （签名）主管警官。

先生，

    谨报告，1937年9月26日上午，发现当前敌对行动爆发时留在杨树浦路中国肥皂公司（China Soap Company）外的三台工部局公共工程处（P.W.D S.M.C）所属压路机中的一台已被带走，而另一台则停在路拱中央，严重阻碍交通。随后的查询显示，大约在1937年9月25日午夜12点，在中国肥皂公司雇用的巡捕房华籍警员第138号（R.P.W.138）听到这三台压路机的引擎启动，他从大门和其水泥支柱之间向内窥视，注意到三台压路机中最小的一台正被身穿制服的日本人向东驾驶离开，无法确定是日本海军陆战队（J.N.L.P.）还是正规军。与此同时，该伙其他成员也试图移走另外两台，但在将最大的一台开到路拱中央并熄火后，这伙人放弃了它们。1937年9月26日上午11点30分，日籍侦探第42号（J.D.S.42）访问了位于平凉路的日本海军陆战队总部，向野口上尉（Capt. Noguchi）报告了上述情况，后者回答说，这台压路机可能是被军方当局带到了日本机场，因为他没有发出关于移除它的指示。他进一步表示，如果是这种情况，财产会得到妥善保管，并在稍后归还原位。1937年9月27日上午6点，在巡逻时发现剩余的两台压路机也被移走，查询显示它们是由日本军方当局在今天凌晨天亮时自行驱动移走，并沿杨树浦路向东运去。

（签名）
9月27日

I.O. O. O.
抄送：秘书处副处长（D.C. (S)）
     "   X. (D)

                                        先生，
                                        （签名）
                                        约翰·克里顿（John Crighton）

II,
At 9.45, am. 22/ /37, t... ... on passing Mr Klien's
house situated at No 335 Sinking Road, I observed Japanese
soldiers in the yard, upon entering the house five Japanese
soldiers, five Japs. and two male Chinese with their hands
tied behind their backs were encountered in the downstairs front
room, one of the soldiers was armed with a bayonet and was
knocking the glass panel out of an inner door.
Immediately upon entering I asked the Japanese Constables the
reason for the soldiers action, and they explained that they were
searching for Chinese. The soldiers desisted from doing further
damage whilst I was present and after a few moments left the
house and went into the roadway where I attempted to negotiate
for the release of the two men explaining that one of them was
employed at the house which was foreign property.
It was also pointed out that a note of identification had been
given to one of the men by J.P.S. 149, but they ignored same and
marched the two men off.
Further enquiries ascertained that the four soldiers had observed
Mr Klien's coolie on the premises and had come in to investigate
and through the medium of two Chinese speaking Military Police
who also arrived on the scene, had asked how many Chinese were
present, to which the coolie had replied that he was alone, not
being satisfied with answer given they searched the outhouses and
found the second Chinese, apparently this angered the soldiers
and caused them to break into the house with intent to search
all rooms.
Mr Klien was communicated with and it was elicited that the
second coolie was formerly employed at a Chinese school, which

Sir,
At 9-30 a.m. Sept. 22nd. a Japanese Marine officer approached F.S. Newell where he was on duty with two S.P.Cs. at the Shanghai Tramway Coy's Depot, Yangtsepoo Road, and requested him to accompany him in his car to Marine Headquarters, Whashing Road.
At Headquarters F.S. Newell was subjected to questioning as to why he was on duty near to the O.S.K. Wharf. Being informed by F.S. Newell his duty was to watch the Tram Depot opposite, the officer said that the O.S.K. Wharf was secret and would he inform his officer in charge to keep policemen away from vicinity of O.S.K. Wharf and that the Japanese Marines were quite capable of looking after any property in the vicinity.
F.S. Newell was detained at Whashing Road for about seven minutes, then allowed to walk back to his station.
In the meantime, the two S.P.Cs. had reported to the station.
This Tram Depot guard was being performed during daytime since 17/9/37. On that date the guard was sent off by Japanese authorities because of closing of roads in vicinity temporarily.
Premises, Lane 120, House 5, Baikal Road, were partially destroyed by a bomb during the evening of 11/9/37. Portion of these premises were occupied by Assistant Warder Knight of Ward Road Gaol, who visited the premises on 21/9/37, when he found that the contents, etc., were more or less intact. However, upon again visiting the premises at 1 p.m. on 22/9/37 he saw two Japanese soldiers inside the premises, which had

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.

Yulin road Station,
REPORT
Date 22/9/37

Subject Re Japanese soldiers entering Foreign premises at No 335
Pingliang Road.

Made by L.S. Rhodes. Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,
At 10.5.am. 22/9/37, F.S. Phillips reported to the station
that Japanese soldiers had entered a foreign dwelling house
situated at No.335 Pingliang road, J.D.S. 149, D... White, and the
undersigned attended but on arrival it was found that the soldiers
had left.

Subsequent enquiries ascertained that the house in question is
owned by Mr Eliene, Director of Chinese Study for the S.M.C., but
he left the house after the outbreak of hostilities, and a Chinese
coolie named You Lou S , remained behind to look after the premises.
At about 9.45.am. 22/9/37 four Japanese soldiers entered the grounds
by a length of galvanized sheeting from fence situated at the
east side of the building, finding all entrances to the house
locked they smashed a pane of glass in a front window but were
unable to enter due to the fact that the window was also protected
by a shutter which was bolted on the inside.
They then smashed another front window and inserted their hands
through the opening and released the catch, climbed through and
entered a front sitting room. Apparently the coolie arrived on the
scene at this juncture and asked them to leave, but it is doubtful
whether they understood him because they answered him in Japanese
which he did not understand. The coolie added that he did not see
them search any drawers etc, neither did they do any damage to the
contents of the room, or carry away any property. Two J.M.Cs.
arrived on the scene before the soldiers left and spoke to them
for a few minutes, then all of them left the premises.
Apart from the broken windows every thing appeared to be in order,
Police nailed up the damaged fence and the coolie was given a note
written in Japanese characters explaining that the property was

主题：关于日本士兵进入平凉路335号外籍人士住宅一事。

制作人：L.S. Rhodes。转发人 [签名]

先生，
1937年9月22日上午10点05分，F.S. Phillips 向警署报告称，日本士兵进入了一栋位于平凉路335号的外籍人士住宅，业主为 J.D.S. 149, D... White，下署名者随即前往，但到达时发现士兵已离开。

后续调查查明，涉案房屋归工部局汉文处处长 Eliene 先生所有，但他在战事爆发后离开了该房屋，留下一名名为 You Lou S (音译) 的华人苦力看守房屋。
1937年9月22日上午9点45分左右，四名日本士兵通过建筑物东侧围栏上的一块镀锌铁皮进入院内，发现房屋所有入口均锁闭后，他们砸碎了前窗的一块玻璃，但因窗户内部还装有插销固定的百叶窗而未能进入。
随后他们砸碎了另一扇前窗，将手伸入开口处解开扣锁，爬进屋内，进入了一间前客厅。显然，苦力此时赶到现场并请他们离开，但他们是否听懂不得而知，因为他们用日语回答，而苦力听不懂。苦力补充说，他没看到他们搜查抽屉等物，他们也未损坏房内物品或带走任何财产。两名日本宪兵（J.M.Cs.）在士兵离开前赶到现场，与他们交谈了几分钟，随后所有人离开了该处。
除了破碎的窗户外，一切似乎井然有序，警方钉好了受损的围栏，并给苦力一张用日文书写的纸条，说明该房产为

September 22nd, 1937.
Subject Japanese Marines enter the Wing On Textile Manufacturing Company
Limited's Mill at No.140 Seoul Road.
Made by D.S.I. Watson. Forwarded [Signature]

Sir,
At 2-50pm. on 22/9/37 a telephone message was received
from an Indian Watchman to the effect that Japanese Marines
were removing property from the Wing On Textile Manufacturing
Company Limited's Mill at No.140 Seoul Road.
This Mill being the property of the Wing On Company, a
British Registered Company, I proceeded at once to that
address with J.P.C.s 148 and 5.
At the corner of Lay Road and Yangtszepoo Road a motor
truck was observed proceeding East On Yangtszepoo Road. This
truck was carrying ten bales of cotton, and was manned by
five Japanese civilians and four Japanese in the uniform of
Reservists, without arms.
The truck was stopped, and the occupants stated that they
had removed the cotton from the above mill. The truck, a
new "Studebaker", bore no licence plates but had the number
"47" painted over the mudguards.
I then proceeded to the Mill, where the gates were
found to be wide open. In the compound were three Japanese
in the uniforms of Reservists. They stated that they were
removing the property on the instructions of the officer
commanding the detachment of the J.N.L.P. on Baikal Road
near Dalny Road.
The Police party then left the Mill, and on leaving
it was observed that two other trucks were loading material
from the Dah Wha Printing and Dyeing Company, located in the
same compound and at the rear of the Mill. These trucks
appeared to be manned by Japanese civilians. One other truck,
the property of the Shanghai Cotton Mill, was seen approaching

1937年9月22日。
主题：日本海军陆战队进入首尔路140号永安纺织制造有限公司工厂。
制作人：副督察 Watson。转发人 [签名]

先生，
1937年9月22日下午2点50分，接到一名印度看守的电话消息，称日本海军陆战队正在从首尔路140号永安纺织制造有限公司工厂搬走财产。
鉴于该工厂属于英资注册企业永安公司所有，我立即偕同印捕（J.P.Cs.）148号和5号前往该地址。
在雷路（Lay Road）与杨树浦路交叉口，观察到一辆卡车沿杨树浦路向东行驶。该卡车载有十包棉花，车上人员包括五名日本平民和四名身穿预备役制服但未携带武器的日本人。
卡车被拦停，车内人员称他们是从上述工厂搬出棉花。该卡车是一辆新的“斯图贝克”（Studebaker）牌，未挂车牌，但在挡泥板上漆有数字“47”。
随后我前往工厂，发现大门敞开。院内有三名身穿预备役制服的日本人。他们称是奉驻大连路附近贝加尔路的日本海军陆战队（J.N.L.P.）分队指挥官之命搬运财产。
警方随后离开工厂，离开时观察到另外两辆卡车正在装载同一院内、工厂后方的大华印染公司（Dah Wha Printing and Dyeing Company）的材料。这些卡车似乎由日本平民驾驶。另见一辆属于上海棉纺厂的卡车正驶来

When returning to this station via Pingliang Road, the truck with the ten bales of cotton was seen proceeding West on Pingliang Road from Glen Road.
Indian Watchmen named Ganda Singh and Hayara Singh had then arrived at Yangtsepoo Station, and they reported as follows:
They are private watchmen employed to look after the Mill, and at about 9am. on 22/9/37 they heard someone knocking on the iron gates, apparently with the butts of rifles. They opened the gates, and two motor trucks with 12 or 14 Japanese Marines, all armed with rifles or pistols, entered the compound. The two watchmen raised their arms above their heads when the Marines left the trucks and approached them, and they were told in English to sit at the rear of the godown, where they were unable to see the compound. They did so, and six of the party remained with them.
At various times during the day they heard motor trucks enter and leave the compound.
At about 2-30pm. 22/9/37 a Japanese Reservist in uniform spoke to them in Chinese and English, and they explained that they wanted some food. After a short consultation with the others, the Reservist told them that they could go. They accordingly proceeded to the China Import and Export Lumber Company, Yangtsepoo Road, where they telephoned to this station.
Special Branch was informed, and there being no confirmation that this Mill was British Property, I

D:- September 17th, 1937.
25 / 37
Subject Motor car No.8740 damaged by Japanese Marines.
Made by . . Watson. Forwarded by Alexander. Hugh E
Sir,
At 9-40am. on 17/9/37, Mr. Kucej, Czechoslovakian, employed
by the Shanghai Power Company and residing at House 7, Lane 358
Glen Road, came to Yangtsepoo Station and reported that two
Japanese Marines had been found tampering with his motor car
in his garage in Lane 358 Glen Road, and that Mr. Crone, British,
also of the Shanghai Power Company, was then with the Marines.
J.P.C. 104 at once accompanied Mr. Kucej to the garage,
followed a few minutes later by D.S.I. Watson.
When J.P.C. 104 arrived at the garage, he questioned the
Marines, and they denied that they had tampered with the car.
They gave their names as Marines Tokuda and Okura, and they
then left the premises. They were fully dressed in uniform
but carried no arms.
Enquiries show that at about 9-35am. on 17/9/37 Mr. Kucej
and Mr. Crone arrived at the garage, the door of which had been
left open, to examine Mr. Kucej's car, an "Essex" Saloon, Licence
No.8740. On entering the garage they discovered the two Marines
in the act of removing the front wheel, the bolts
having already been removed. The doors had been locked, and
the windscreen had been broken open same. The ignition wires
were pulled out from the dash-board, and the oil and fuel
indicator was lying on the rear seat. The Marines had removed
their tunics and equipment, and these were also in the rear of
the car.
After Mr. Kucej departed to report the matter to this
Station, the Marines dressed themselves, and were ready to
leave when J.P.C. 104 arrived.
D.S.I. Watson and J.P.C. 104 accompanied by Mr. Kucej and

事由 第8740号汽车被日本海军陆战队损坏。
制作人 . . 沃森 (Watson)。转呈人 休·E·亚历山大 (Hugh E Alexander)。
先生，
1937年9月17日上午9时40分，受雇于上海电力公司、居住在格伦路（Glen Road）358弄7号的捷克斯洛伐克籍库切伊先生（Mr. Kucej）来到杨树浦巡捕房报案称，有两名日本海军陆战队员在其位于格伦路358弄的车库内摆弄他的汽车，当时同属上海电力公司的英籍克罗恩先生（Mr. Crone）也与这些陆战队员在一起。
警佐（J.P.C.）104号立即陪同库切伊先生前往车库，副督察长（D.S.I.）沃森几分钟后也随后赶到。
当警佐104号到达车库时，他询问了那些陆战队员，他们否认曾摆弄过该车辆。他们报出姓名为德田（Tokuda）和大仓（Okura）陆战队员，随后离开了现场。他们身着全套制服，但未携带武器。
经查，1937年9月17日上午9时35分左右，库切伊先生和克罗恩先生到达车库，车门未锁，目的是检查库切伊先生的一辆“埃塞克斯”（Essex）牌轿车，车牌号为8740。进入车库后，他们发现两名陆战队员正在拆卸前轮，螺栓已被卸下。车门已被锁上，挡风玻璃也被砸破。点火线从仪表板上被拔出，机油和燃油指示器躺在后座上。陆战队员脱下了他们的上衣和装备，这些东西也在汽车后部。
库切伊先生离开去本巡捕房报案后，陆战队员穿好衣服，在警佐104号到达时正准备离开。

Yangtzepoo
D. Sept., 21st. 37.
Subject Sino-Japanese Hostilities in Yangtzepoo District for the
24 hours ending 8am. on 21/9/37.
Made by D.S.I. Watson. Forwarded by
Sir,
At 9am. on 20/9/37 two members of the J.N.L.P. came to
Yangtzepoo Station and asked that the S.F.Brigade be called
to extinguish a fire which had broken out in the Zung Tuh
Cotton Mill (Chinese), No.590 Lianching Road near Point Road,
which they stated had been burning since the evening of
19/9/37. This Mill is within the "Prohibited Area" and the
fire had first been noticed from this station at about 8am.
on 20/9/37.
F.S.Wimsett and J.D.S.42 accompanied the S.F.Brigade to
the scene, where the fire was extinguished within a short
period. Two godowns, two semi-foreign houses and the office
had been completely gutted. The flooring of the Mill itself
had been slightly damaged by cotton wool which had been
placed on the floor and set alight. Apart from this damage,
the machinery had been smashed with heavy instruments, and
the steel frame-netting, also the belting, had been cut.
The origin of the fire is unknown, but it would appear to
have been caused by members of the J.N.L.P., and the machinery
had been deliberately destroyed.
Further to the incident to m/car No.1634 in which D.S.I.
Crighton was involved, he was admitted to the Country Hospital
on 20/9/39 suffering from knee injuries.
Chinese aeroplanes appeared over this
district at approximately 10-50pm. on 20/9/37, and were fired
on by Anti-Aircraft Guns situated in this district. As far
as can be ascertained, no bombs dropped in this district, but
two large explosions were heard from the vicinity of the
Japanese Aerodrome to the East of this district.

事由 截至1937年9月21日上午8时的24小时内杨树浦辖区的中日敌对行动情况。
制作人 副督察长沃森。转呈人
先生，
1937年9月20日上午9时，两名日本海军陆战队（J.N.L.P.）成员来到杨树浦巡捕房，请求呼叫救火会（S.F.Brigade）扑灭位于联兴路（Lianching Road）590号、靠近百老汇路（Point Road）的中和棉纺厂（华资）发生的火灾，他们称该火灾自1937年9月19日晚起一直燃烧。该厂位于“禁区”内，本巡捕房首次注意到火情是在1937年9月20日上午8时左右。
消防监督温姆塞特（F.S.Wimsett）和第42号初级侦探（J.D.S.42）随救火会前往现场，火势在短时间内被扑灭。两座仓库、两栋半西式房屋和办公室被完全烧毁。厂房本身的地板因铺在地上并被点燃的棉花而受到轻微损坏。除上述损坏外，机器被重型器械砸毁，钢制框架网和传动带也被切断。
起火原因不明，但似乎是由日本海军陆战队成员引起，且机器系被故意破坏。
关于副督察长克里顿（Crighton）涉及的第1634号汽车事件，他因膝盖受伤于1939年9月20日被送入乡村医院（Country Hospital）。
1937年9月20日晚上10时50分左右，中国飞机出现在本辖区上空，并遭到位于本辖区的高射炮射击。据查，本辖区未投下炸弹，但在本辖区以东的日本机场附近听到两次巨大爆炸声。

Made by D.S. 24 White Forwarded by
Sir,
At about 12.50.p.m. on the 14/9/37 a party of six Japanese
Marines under an officer were seen to enter Messrs Moutres.
Baikal Rd. Inspector Hanafuji and the undersigned proceeded to the
above factory and ascertained from the Officer that he was simply
checking the number of persons still living in the district. When
it was pointed out to him that the premises were British property
and that the British flag was flying over the building signifying
the building as being such, he regretted the mistake stating that
he had not observed the Union Jack (a very large one) flying from
the building.
At 7.30.a.m. an Indian watchman employed at "Woodworths & Co",
No. 60 Tanyang Rd reported that during the afternoon of the 13/9/37
fifteen Japanese Marines had entered the factory and told him to
leave as they were going to live there. About two hours later the
Marines left and on making an inspection of the premises the watch-
man found that a safe and several desks had been broken open and
their contents strewn over the floors. These premises are flying
the American Flag but are in the Special Branch Factory list as
being owned by Chinese; this is the third report of Japanese
Marines entering this factory.
At 7.30.p.m. 14/9/37 airplane(s) were heard flying over the
district and was met with anti-aircraft gun fire resulting in it
moving away; although it could be heard flying over Chapel all
during the evening. Heavy machine gun and rifle fire was heard
coming from over the northern boundary of the district throughout
the evening, and early morning.
B. D. i/e.

榆林路巡捕房，
第21号报告
日期 1937年9月15日 19
事由 截至1937年9月15日上午7时榆林辖区的情况
制作人 第24号侦探长怀特 (White) 转呈人
先生，
1937年9月14日中午12时50分左右，有人看到六名日本海军陆战队员在一名军官带领下进入莫特雷斯公司（Messrs Moutres，音译），位于贝加尔路（Baikal Rd.）。花藤井（Hanafuji，音译）巡长和本人前往上述工厂，并从该军官处获悉，他只是在核查仍居住在该地区的人数。当向他指出该处所为英国产业，且建筑物上悬挂着英国国旗以表明其性质时，他对这一错误表示遗憾，称未注意到建筑物上悬挂的米字旗（一面非常大的旗帜）。
上午7时30分，坦阳路（Tanyang Rd.，音译）60号“伍德沃斯公司”（Woodworths & Co.）的一名印度更夫报告称，1937年9月13日下午，十五名日本海军陆战队员进入工厂，命令他离开，因为他们要住在那里。大约两小时后，陆战队员离开，经检查，更夫发现一个保险箱和几张书桌被撬开，里面的物品散落在地板上。这些场所悬挂美国国旗，但在特别股工厂名单中列为华人所有；这是第三次有关日本海军陆战队员进入该工厂的报告。
1937年9月14日晚上7时30分，听到飞机飞越辖区上空，并遭遇高射炮火击退，使其飞离；尽管整晚仍能听到其在教堂上空飞行的声音。整晚及清晨，听到重机枪和步枪射击声来自辖区北部边界方向。
B. D. i/e.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No.
Yangtsepoo Station
REPORT
Date September 14th, 1937.
Subject Sung Sing No.6 Cotton Mill gutted by fire.
Made by L.S.I. Watson. Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,

I beg to report that at 10-25am. on 14/9/37 C.C.R. informed Yulin Road Station that a fire had been observed in the vicinity of Lay Road and Hochien Road.

A party consisting of D.I. Hutton, SII. Biggs, D.S. White and J.D.S. 149 Urakami visited that area and discovered that the fire was inside the No.6 Sung Sing Cotton Mill. A party of Japanese Marines were observed at their sandbagged post of Hochien Road Bridge.

The S.F.Brigade, Y'Poo Station, were summoned by D.I. Hutton, but on arrival, they were refused permission from the Marines to operate.

The Marines explained through J.D.S. 149 that they were acting on instructions from Commander Yasuda of the Japanese Naval Landing Party.

At 5pm. on 14/9/37 it was observed that the fire had burnt itself out, the premises being completely gutted.

The origin of the fire is unknown, there being no shelling in this vicinity.

I am, Sir,
Your Obedient Servant,
[Signature] Watson

D.D.O. "D"
D.S.I.

事由 松盛第六棉纺厂被大火烧毁。
制作人 初级副督察长沃森。转呈人 [签名]

先生，

谨报告，1937年9月14日上午10时25分，中央无线电接收站（C.C.R.）通知榆林路巡捕房，在雷路（Lay Road，音译）和合信路（Hochien Road，音译）附近发现火情。

由督察赫顿（Hutton）、二级督察比格斯（Biggs）、侦探长怀特和第149号初级侦探浦上（Urakami，音译）组成的小组前往该地区，发现火灾发生在松盛第六棉纺厂内。观察到一群日本海军陆战队员在合信路桥的沙袋哨位处。

督察赫顿召来了杨树浦巡捕房的救火会，但到达后，陆战队员拒绝允许其作业。

陆战队员通过第149号初级侦探解释称，他们是按照日本海军陆战队安田（Yasuda，音译）指挥官的指令行事。

1937年9月14日下午5时，观察到火势自行熄灭，场所被完全烧毁。

起火原因不明，附近没有炮击。

先生，
您的顺从仆人，
[签名] 沃森

Date September 15th, 1937.
Subject Sino-Japanese Hostilities in Yangtsepoo District for 24 hours
ending 6am. on 15/9/37.
Made by D.S.I. Watson. Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,

I beg to report that Yangtsepoo District remained quiet
during daylight on 14/9/37.

A fire broke out in the Sung Sing No.6 Mill, on Hochien
Road near Seoul Road, at about 10am. on 14/9/37. The S.F. Brigade
were called by the Police, but Japanese Marines on duty at
the Hochien Road bridge refused them permission to operate.
The fire burnt itself out at about 8pm. on 14/9/37, the
premises being completely gutted. (Special report attached)

At about 7-55pm. on 14/9/37 Chinese aircraft appeared over
this district, but as far as can be ascertained, no bombs were
dropped. They were fired upon by Anti-Aircraft Guns located in
this district.

I am, Sir,
Your Obedient Servant,
D.F. Watson
D.S.I.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No. Misc.321/37
Wayside Station
Further REPORT No.22
Date. Sept.12, 1937

Subject Incidents resulting from Sino-Japanese Hostilities

Made by...D.S.I.McCahey Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,
At 2.pm.Sept.11th.a party of Japanese Marines were observed loading firewood on to a Motortruck on Baikal Road. The firewood was taken from a Shop No.220 on the South side of the road.
At about 10.30 p.m.11th.an air raid took place over Wayside I District. A bomb was dropped which fell at the corner of Chusan and Ward Road in the roadway.
Very little damage caused by explosion of bomb, due to already damaged condition of premises in the vicinity.
Windows of unoccupied single mens' quarters of Ward Road Gaol damaged and other windows of houses broken, whilst a fire hydrant and Post Office letter box were damaged.
Shrapnel and fragments of anti-aircraft shells resultant from these raids fell into the compound of Wayside Station, the bomb also causing fragments of stone and brick to fall into station compound.
Rifle and machine gun fire heard during the late evening from Northern boundary of Wayside District.

Yours obediently,
[Signature]
D. S. I.

D. D. O. "D" Division.

制作人...副督察长麦卡希 转呈人 [签名]

先生，
9月11日下午2时，观察到一群日本海军陆战队员在贝加尔路将木柴装上一辆卡车。木柴取自路南侧的220号店铺。
9月11日晚上10时30分左右，路边第一辖区发生空袭。一枚炸弹落下，掉在中山路（Chusan）和华德路（Ward Road）交叉口的路面上。
由于附近建筑物已处于受损状态，炸弹爆炸造成的损害很小。
华德路监狱无人居住的单身宿舍窗户受损，其他房屋的窗户破碎，同时一个消防栓和邮政信箱受损。
空袭产生的弹片和高射炮弹碎片落入路边巡捕房大院，炸弹还导致石块和砖块碎片落入巡捕房大院。
深夜时分，听到路边辖区北部边界方向传来步枪和机枪射击声。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
Miss: File No.... 312/37
Yulin Rd. Station,
REPORT
Date.... 14/9/37 .......19
Subject.... Japanese Armed Civilians break and enter the "Wei Tung Ha Kao"
Cotton Mill, No.545 Lay Road.
Made by D. I. Hutton. Forwarded by

Sir, at
At 8.25.a.m. 13/9/37 a private watchman named Sudagar Singh
employed as a watchman at the "Wei Tung" Cotton Mill, No.545 Lay
Road, reported that six Japanese civilians had entered the Mill
premises by climbing over the wall and after threatening him, had
broken into the offices and smashed the safe and desks.
The undersigned accompanied by J.D.S.149 proceeded to the Mill
premises but there, found the iron gates locked and secured. As
the watchman had not returned to the Mill after making his report
the undersigned returned to the station and to ascertain where he
had gone, and after searching round he was located on Chenulpo Rd,
and accompanied the police to the Headquarters of the Japanese
Military Police at the Shanghai No.1 Mill, Y'poo Rd. J.D.S.149
interviewed the police and after an elapse of about 15 minutes,
during which time one of the police left the Headquarters on a
bicycle, and on returning the party proceeded to Lay Rd.
Two Military Police were detailed to accompany the undersigned
to the Mill where upon arrival it was found that the iron gates
had been broken, while one of the side gates was standing wide
open. The police party entered and found from investigation that
about 7.30.a.m. 13/9/37 six Japanese civilians four armed with
pistols, one with a hammer and the other unarmed entered the Mill
premises by scaling the wall round the south east of the factory.
Sudagar Singh the watchman was standing with two other Indians
named Sapuran Singh employed as a watchman at No.300 Meichow Rd
and Tija Singh, watchman of the Sacred Heart Hospital, Ningkuo Rd.
The Japanese approached and informed them to leave the premises
or they would be taken to the Naval Landing Party Headquarters.
The British Flag which was flying from the flag-pole at the front

榆林路捕房，
报告
日期.... 1937年9月14日 .......19
事由.... 日本武装平民闯入并进入雷士德路545号“卫通”纱厂。
具报人 D. I. Hutton。转呈人

先生，
1937年9月13日上午8时25分，一名受雇于雷士德路545号“卫通”（Wei Tung）纱厂担任更夫的私人警卫苏达加尔·辛格（Sudagar Singh）报告称，六名日本平民翻墙进入纱厂厂区，在威胁他之后，闯入办公室并砸坏了保险箱和办公桌。
具报人随同警员编号149前往纱厂厂区，但在那里发现铁门已锁好并加固。由于该更夫在报案后未返回纱厂，具报人返回捕房以查明其去向，经四处搜寻，在陈尔波路（Chenulpo Rd，音译）找到他，随后他陪同警方前往位于杨树浦路上海第一纱厂的日本宪兵队总部。警员编号149会见了宪兵，大约过了15分钟，期间一名宪兵骑自行车离开总部，返回后，一行人便前往雷士德路。
两名宪兵被指派陪同具报人前往纱厂，到达后发现铁门已被破坏，而一扇侧门则大开着。警方进入后经调查发现，1937年9月13日上午7时30分左右，六名日本平民，其中四人持有手枪，一人持有锤子，另一人未持武器，通过攀爬工厂东南侧的围墙进入纱厂厂区。
更夫苏达加尔·辛格当时正与另外两名印度人站在一起，分别是受雇于眉州路300号的更夫萨普兰·辛格（Sapuran Singh）和宁国路圣心医院（Sacred Heart Hospital）的更夫蒂贾·辛格（Tija Singh）。日本人走近并告知他们离开厂区，否则将被带往海军陆战队总部。悬挂在前面的英国国旗

File No....

gots were removed and the watchmen told that the Mill was owned
by Chinese, this information is in accordance with the Special
Branch Factory list but some was recently taken over by the "Wing
On" Company thus making the Factory British property.
An inspection of the premises proved that a large safe in
the general office had been broken open and the contents ransacked,
drawers in the desks were similarly treated. The locks and bolts
on the iron gates were broken off and left on the ground. It would
appear that during the absence of the S.M.P. requesting the assis-
tance of the Military Police the breakers were informed of the
visit and made a hasty escape.
Inspector Manafuji Senior Japanese Officer at Yulin Road
Station was informed of the breaking and stated that such an inci-
dent could not be helped as the Mill was Chinese owned. The Acting
Commissioner of Police visited Yulin Rd Station during the fore-
noon and upon being informed of the incident he instructed that
two J.P.C.s be posted on the premises as the watchman failed to
return to his duty and was too scared to return unless police were
kept on duty.
Sudagar Singh was later located and a statement obtained
giving the particulars. Sapuran Singh was also located and a state-
ment obtained. In this statement it will be seen that Sapuran
Singh identified one of the Japanese civilians as an electrician
employed at the Shanghai No.4 Cotton Mill, Pingliang Rd. Sapuran
Singh was formerly employed at the Shanghai No.4 Mill and is there-
fore in a position to identify the man.
No estimate of the damage done to the Mill can be given
until the management returns to make an inspection.
D. I.
D.D.O. "D".

D.C. "Div".

旗杆上的旗帜被取下，更夫们被告知该纱厂为中国人所有，这一信息与特科（Special Branch）的工厂清单相符，但该厂最近已被“永安”（Wing On）公司接管，从而使该工厂成为英国财产。
对现场的检查证明，总办公室内的一个大保险箱被撬开，内部物品被洗劫，办公桌的抽屉也遭到同样对待。铁门上的锁和插销被折断并留在地上。看来，在工部局警务处（S.M.P.）请求宪兵协助期间，闯入者得知了此次来访并匆忙逃离。
榆林路捕房的日本高级警官Manafuji巡官获悉了这起闯入事件，并表示此类事件无法避免，因为该纱厂为中国人所有。代理警务总监上午视察了榆林路捕房，在获悉此事后，他指示在该场所派驻两名日本巡捕（J.P.C.s），因为更夫未能返岗，且除非有警察执勤，否则他因过于恐惧而不敢返回。
后来找到了苏达加尔·辛格并获取了其详细情况的供词。也找到了萨普兰·辛格并获取了供词。从这份供词中可以看出，萨普兰·辛格指认其中一名日本平民是受雇于平凉路上海第四纱厂的一名电工。萨普兰·辛格此前曾在上海第四纱厂工作，因此能够指认此人。
在管理层返回进行检查之前，无法评估纱厂遭受的损失。
D. I.
D区副总监。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of..Sudagar Singh............................................................
native of.....India................................................taken by me....W.S. Rhodes...............................
at Yulin Road Station the....13/9/37................and interpreted by ..P.C.275.......................

My name Sudagar Singh, son of Jodh Singh nativ - of the village
Burag Rai Ka, Amritsar Punjab India, and at present residing at
the "Wei Tung" cotton mill No 845 Lay Road ,where I am also
employed as a private watchman.
At about 7.30.a.m. 13/9/37 I was on duty at the mill compound
when I observed six Japanese civilians climbing over the south
wall, four of them were armed with pistols and one carried a
hammer. Immediately upon entering th compound one of the intruders
who was unarmed approached me and two of my friends namely Teja
Singh and Sapuran Singh, and addressing us in the Chinese
language ordered that we leave the premises at once because it
was a Chinese owned concern and very dangerous to stay any longer,
the spokesman also added that if I or my two friends failed to
obey the order our hands would be tied behind our backs and we
would be taken to the Japanese Headquarters.
I and my friends at once prepared to leave the premises and before
I had passed through the outer gate I saw one of the Japanese
pull down the British flag which was flying over the main entrance.
I at once reported the occurrence to Yulin Road Police Station
Upon returning to the mill in company with Police Officers and
members of the Japanese military I observed that drawers, cupboards,
etc in every office had been ransacked and the contents had been
strewn all over the floor, the safe had been smashed open and the
contents were missing, and numerous windows and glass panels had
been smashed. The British flag also could not be found .
All this destruction took place after my being compelled to leave
the premises,and whilst I was reporting the occurrence t the Polic

Signed,

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
警方调查报告。

以下是..苏达加尔·辛格（Sudagar Singh）............................................................的陈述，
籍贯.....印度................................................由我....W.S. Rhodes...............................于....1937年9月13日................在榆林路捕房录取，并由 ..警员编号275.......................翻译。

我叫苏达加尔·辛格，父亲是乔德·辛格（Jodh Singh），籍贯印度旁遮普邦阿姆利则（Amritsar）布拉格·拉伊·卡村（Burag Rai Ka），现居住并受雇于雷士德路845号“卫通”纱厂，担任私人更夫。
1937年9月13日上午7时30分左右，我正在纱厂大院内执勤，此时我观察到六名日本平民翻越南墙，其中四人持有手枪，一人携带锤子。进入大院后，一名未持武器的闯入者立即走近我和我的两位朋友，即泰贾·辛格（Teja Singh）和萨普兰·辛格（Sapuran Singh），用中文对我们说话，命令我们立即离开该场所，因为这是中国人的产业，继续停留非常危险，发言人还补充说，如果我和我的朋友不服从命令，我们的手将被绑在背后，并被带往日本总部。
我和朋友们立即准备离开该场所，在我穿过外大门之前，我看到一名日本人扯下了悬挂在主入口上方的英国国旗。我随即向榆林路捕房报告了此事。
在与警官和日本军方人员一同返回纱厂时，我观察到每个办公室里的抽屉、橱柜等都被翻乱，内容物散落在地板上，保险箱被砸开，里面的东西不见了，许多窗户和玻璃板也被打碎。英国国旗也不见了。
所有这些破坏行为都发生在我被迫离开该场所之后，以及我向警方报告此事期间

签名，

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Sapuran Singh
native of India taken by me S. Rhodes,
at Yulin Road Station on the 13/9/37 and interpreted by S.P.C.275.

My name is Sapuran Singh son of Massa Singh native of the village
Bopa Ra, in the district of Lahore India, and at present residing
and employed at a Chinese rubber factory situated at No 300 Miech-
ow Road.

At about 7.30.a.m. 13/9/37 I Sudagar Singh and one named Teja
Singh were standing in the compound of the "Wei "Tung" cotton
mill No 545 Lay Road when I saw about six Japanese civilians
climb over the wall of the mill and enter the compound, as they
approached I noticed that four of them were armed with pistols
a fifth carried a hammer, and one was unarmed.
The intruders came to where we were standing and the unarmed man
addressing us in the Chinese language ordered us to leave the
premises at once, failing which we would be tied with our hands
behind our backs and taken to the Japanese Naval Headquarters.
I in company with my companions immediately left the mill and
proceeded to Yulin Road Police station where the occurrence was
reported.

I was able to recognize one of the Japanese as an employee of
the No 4 Shanghai Cotton Mill Pingliang Road, he (the Japanese) was
an electrical engineer within the above mill when I was employed as
a watchman there.

Signed.

以下是萨普兰·辛格（Sapuran Singh）的陈述
籍贯印度，由我 S. Rhodes 于1937年9月13日在榆林路捕房录取，并由特别巡捕编号275翻译。

我叫萨普兰·辛格，父亲是马萨·辛格（Massa Singh），籍贯印度拉合尔（Lahore）地区博帕·拉村（Bopa Ra），现居住并受雇于眉州路300号的一家中国橡胶厂。

1937年9月13日上午7时30分左右，我与苏达加尔·辛格和一名叫泰贾·辛格的人站在雷士德路545号“卫通”纱厂的大院里，这时我看到大约六名日本平民翻过纱厂的围墙进入大院，当他们走近时，我注意到其中四人持有手枪，第五人携带一把锤子，一人未持武器。
闯入者来到我们站立的地方，那名未持武器的人用中文对我们说话，命令我们立即离开该场所，否则我们将被双手反绑并带往日本海军总部。
我与同伴们立即离开了纱厂，前往榆林路捕房报告了此事。

我能认出其中一名日本人是平凉路上海第四纱厂的雇员，当我在那里担任更夫时，他（该日本人）是上述纱厂的一名电气工程师。

签名。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Teja Singh
native of India taken by me D.S. 114 Rhodes.
at Yulin Rd Stn on the 14/9/37 and interpreted by S.P.C. 275.

My name is Teja Singh, son of Jawala Singh, native of the
village of Malu Wal, Post Office Bhi Khi, in the district of
Shekhu Pur, Punjab, India, at present residing at the Sacred Heart
Hospital, Ningkou Rd where I am also employed as a private watch-
man.

At about 7.a.m 13/9/37 I came to No.545 Lay Rd to visit my
friend arriving there at about 7.15.a.m. At about 7.30.a.m. 13/9,
I together with Sugagar Singh and Bajuran Singh were standing in
the compound of the "Wei Tung" Cotton Mill No.545 Lay Rd when I
observed six male Japanese Civilians climb over the South wall of
the Mill and enter the compound. As they approached us I observed
that four of the men were armed with pistols, and one with a ham-
mer, one of the intruders who was unarmed then addressed me and
my companions in the Chinese language and ordered us to leave the
premises immediately, failing which they threatened they would
tie our hands behind our backs and we should be taken to the Jap-
anese Naval Headquarters.

I and my companions at once left the Mill and together
proceeded to Yulin Rd Police Station to report the incident.

This is my true Statement
Signed Teja Singh.

以下是泰贾·辛格（Teja Singh）的陈述
籍贯印度，由我 D.S. 114 Rhodes 于1937年9月14日在榆林路捕房录取，并由特别巡捕编号 275翻译。

我叫泰贾·辛格，父亲是贾瓦拉·辛格（Jawala Singh），籍贯印度旁遮普邦谢库普尔（Shekhu Pur）区马尔乌瓦尔村（Malu Wal），邮局地址为比基（Bhi Khi），现居住并受雇于宁国路圣心医院，担任私人更夫。

1937年9月13日上午7点左右，我来到雷士德路545号拜访朋友，约于上午7时15分到达。1937年9月13日上午7时30分左右，我与苏加加尔·辛格（Sugagar Singh）和巴朱兰·辛格（Bajuran Singh）一起站在雷士德路545号“卫通”纱厂的大院里，这时我观察到六名日本男性平民翻过纱厂的南墙进入大院。当他们向我们走近时，我观察到其中四人持有手枪，一人持有锤子，一名未持武器的闯入者随后用中文对我及同伴说话，命令我们立即离开该场所，否则他们威胁要将我们的手绑在背后，并将我们带往日本海军总部。

我和同伴们立即离开了纱厂，一同前往榆林路捕房报告此事。

这是我的真实陈述
签名 泰贾·辛格。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
5039
Waygloo Station, ?
FURTHER REPORT No. 16.
Date Sept. 7th. 19 37.
Subject Incidents arising from Sino-Japanese Hostilities.
Made by D.S.I. McCahey. Forwarded by [Signature].

Sir,
Whilst on patrol during the forenoon of Sept. 6th. the
undersigned observed a detachment of the Japanese Naval Landing
Party searching for an alleged sniper in the three partially
burned out blocks bounded on North by East Seward Road, East
by Kungping Road, South by Broadway East and on West by Hwakee
Road.
Returning along East Seward Road at 11 a.m. the C.P.O.
Letter Box situated at corner of Kungping and East Seward Road
was open (forced) and several pieces of mail matter strewn about
the crossing, envelopes torn open and contents apparently read.
As this box was in order on proceeding West the undersigned
suspects this raiding party of having broken it open. They also
entered, by force, several houses, previously known to be
intact, and when seen marching North to their posts, were
carrying at least one Chinese suitcase.

Yours obediently,
[Signature]
D. S. I.

D.D.O. "D" Division.
Officer i/c Special Branch.
D.C. (Divisions).
[Handwritten notes]

威古路（Waygloo，音译）捕房，?
第16号进一步报告。
日期 1937年9月7日。
事由 中日敌对行动引发的事件。
具报人 副督察 McCahey。转呈人 [签名]。

先生，
9月6日上午巡逻期间，具报人观察到一支日本海军陆战队分队正在搜寻一名所谓的狙击手，搜索区域为三个部分烧毁的街区，北至东熙华德路，东至公平路，南至百老汇路（东段），西至霍山路（Hwakee Road）。
上午11点沿东熙华德路返回时，位于公平路与东熙华德路拐角处的中央邮政信箱（C.P.O. Letter Box）是开着的（被强行打开），几件邮件散落在十字路口，信封被撕开，内容显然已被阅读。由于具报人在向西行进时该信箱完好无损，具报人怀疑是这支搜查队将其撬开。他们还强行进入了数所此前已知完好无损的房屋，当看到他们向北 marching 回到岗位时，他们至少提着一个中式手提箱。

此致，
[签名]
副督察

D区副总监。
特科主管官员。
分区侦探长。
[手写笔记]

No. 1. Sept. 1, 9 37
Looting by Members of Japanese Naval Landing Party.

D.S.I. McCahy.

Sir,
At 9 a.m. August 31st. the undersigned observed three members of the J.N.L. Party in a, at present vacated, Russian sweet water (Kvass) shop at 1030 Broadway East, loading bottles of said water on to a tricycle believed to belong to Geddes, & Co. 266 Ward Road. A fourth marine was just arriving by bicycle.
On reporting to station a party of police including Inspt. Lees, F.S. Booth, the undersigned, and J.P.S. 26 and two S.P.Cs. proceeded along Broadway East and witnessed four marines, armed with pistols and bayonets, with two bicycles and one tricycle, the latter loaded with three wooden cases of Russian Sweet Waters, leave premises 1030 Broadway East and proceed in an Easterly direction, probably to O.S.K. Wharf billets.
Entry was gained by looters through the broken plate glass window in front but the goods were handed out via a small grille window at rear, and packed in cases on tricycle, the latter having been passed through the side door leading to rear of House 28, Lane 130, Kungping Road. The bottom left panel of this door having been broken in to allow the latch to be opened.
Attention is drawn to suspicion that this same door was used when adjoining premises 27, Lane 13C, Kungping Road, were looted. (Please see Central Misc. 620/37 Looting, Ref. No. 13. Wayside Misc. No. 363/37.)

Yours obediently,
(签名)
D. S. I.

D.D.O. "D" Division.
Officer i/c Special Branch.

第1号。1937年9月1日
日本海军陆战队成员抢劫。

副督察 McCahy。

先生，
8月31日上午9时，具报人观察到三名日本海军陆战队（J.N.L.）成员在东百老汇路1030号一家目前空置的俄罗斯甜水（克瓦斯/Kvass）店内，将所述甜水瓶装上一辆据信属于盖德斯公司（Geddes, & Co.，华德路266号）的三轮车。第四名海军陆战队员正骑自行车赶到。
在向捕房报告后，包括利斯（Lees）巡官、高级警员 Booth、具报人、日本巡捕编号26和两名特别巡捕在内的一队警察沿东百老汇路前行，目睹四名手持手枪和刺刀的海军陆战队员，带着两辆自行车和一辆三轮车，后者装载着三木箱俄罗斯甜水，离开东百老汇路1030号的 premises 并向东行进，可能前往大阪商船会社（O.S.K.）码头的营房。
抢劫者通过前面破碎的玻璃窗进入，但货物是通过后面的一个小格栅窗口递出的，并装在三轮车的箱子里，该三轮车曾被推过通往公平路130弄28号房屋后部的侧门。该门左下角的面板被打破，以便打开门闩。
提请注意的是，有人怀疑当公平路13C弄27号的相邻房屋被抢劫时，也使用了同一扇门。（请参阅中央杂项 620/37 抢劫案，参考号 13。路边杂项号 363/37。）

此致，
(签名)
副督察

D区副总监。
特科主管官员。
